signals.title: [Bugfix][V1] Restore hybrid GDN prefix-cache hits under MTP spec decoding
signals.text: ## Purpose On **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B** with MTP speculative decoding, a replay of a cached prompt never reaches the depth the prefix cache could give it, and prompts whose length is a multiple of the hash unit get **no hit at all**. Measured live before this change, with a 1072-token GDN page and `--prefix-match-unit 67`: | prompt | cached tokens on replay | ceiling | |---|---|---| | 1072 | **0** | 938 | | 2000 | **0** | 1876 | | 2144 | **0** | 2010 | | 3000 | 1072 | 2881 | | 3500 | 2144 | 3417 | ### Root cause Three rules compose badly. A lookup caps at `prompt_len - 1`, because the last token must be recomputed for logits. The MTP/EAGLE drafter then rewinds the hit one hash unit (67) further. But the producer publishes the GDN state at the prompt's own tail boundary, `prompt_len // 67 * 67`, which is at or above the cap — so the recurrent group cannot resume where the rewind lands, and the coordinator intersects the two groups down to the previous full page (or to zero). The same cap breaks the full-attention side whenever `prompt_len` is a multiple of 67 — and every page multiple is, since `1072 = 16 × 67`. Its partial-tail entry is registered at `prompt_len // 67 * 67 == prompt_len`, which the `- 1` cap excludes, so full attention itself matches nothing below the page boundary and the hybrid hit collapses to 0. That is the `1072 → 0`, `2144 → 0` row above. ### Fix Write-side only, all of it gated on MTP/EAGLE plus fine-grained hashing being active: - `mamba_state_cache_position(num_tokens, block_size, hash_block_size)` in `kv_cache_utils.py`: `unit = min(hash_block_size, block_size)`, returns `(num_tokens - 1 - unit) // unit * unit` — the position a replay actually lands on. - `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` stops a prefill chunk there, so that state exists to be published. It is an **extra** stop; the existing block-aligned stops stay. Replacing them lets intermediate chunks end off-grid and re-triggers the state poisoning of #43559 (14 tests in `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` fail that way). - `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` publishes the GDN state there instead of at the prompt tail. - `FullAttentionManager._cache_partial_tail_block` additionally publishes `(prompt_len - 1) // 67 * 67`, the deepest tail a replay can reach. The unshifted tail is kept, because requests that *extend* this prompt have a higher cap and can still match it. - `MambaManager` reports a block-aligned prompt end as unreachable through a new `reachable_block_mask()` argument, so that state is not cached in any retention mode: no lookup can land at or past a prompt's own end, and the rewound state below it is where consumers land. Guarded on the latter being cached. The rewound position is read from one `MambaManager` helper rather than recomputed per caller, and keys off whether the engine runs a drafter rather than the per-group `use_eagle` bit, which is only set on groups that take the drop. Without the last item the page multiples stay at 0 no matter where the GDN state sits: the producer had the state at 938 / 2010 / 3082, but full attention offered nothing below 1072 / 2144 / 3216 for the intersection to meet. ## Test Plan ```bash # unit pytest tests/v1/core -q # e2e: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, 4x B200, MTP 3 tokens, sub-page hashing vllm serve $QWEN35_122B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --spec-method mtp --spec-tokens 3 --prefix-match-unit 67 --port 8110 ``` Hit depth is read from the `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` delta of a replay: a token-id prompt of an exact length is sent three times and the second and third deltas are the cached length. 132 lengths from 1 to 15k were swept — every page multiple with its `+1`, `+unit-1`, `+unit`, `+unit+1` neighbours, plus scattered lengths. Two further passes cover the configurations where the patch must do nothing, and quality was checked on top of real hits. ## Test Result (1) Hit Length Boundary All 132 lengths land exactly on the replay ceiling `(P - 1 - 67) // 67 * 67`. Page-boundary neighbourhoods, where the old code either missed entirely or fell back a full page: | prompt | position | before | after | replay ceiling | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1072 | k*1072 | 0 | 938 | 938 | | 1073 | k*1072 + 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 | | 1138 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 | | 1139 | k*1072 + unit | 0 | 1005 | 1005 | | 1140 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 0 | 1072 | 1072 | | 2144 | k*1072 | 0 | 2010 | 2010 | | 2145 | k*1072 + 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 | | 2210 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 | | 2211 | k*1072 + unit | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 | | 2212 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 1072 | 2144 | 2144 | | 3216 | k*1072 | 0 | 3082 | 3082 | | 3217 | k*1072 + 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 | | 3282 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 | | 3283 | k*1072 + unit | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 | | 3284 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 2144 | 3216 | 3216 | | 5360 | k*1072 | 0 | 5226 | 5226 | | 5361 | k*1072 + 1 | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 | | 5426 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 | | 5427 | k*1072 + unit | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 | | 5428 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 4288 | 5360 | 5360 | | 10720 | k*1072 | 7504 | 10586 | 10586 | | 10721 | k*1072 + 1 | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 | | 10786 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 | | 10787 | k*1072 + unit | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 | | 10788 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 9648 | 10720 | 10720 | Other lengths: | prompt | before | after | ceiling | |---|---|---|---| | 500 | 0 | 402 | 402 | | 999 | 0 | 871 | 871 | | 2000 | 0 | 1876 | 1876 | | 3000 | 1072 | 2881 | 2881 | | 3500 | 2144 | 3417 | 3417 | | 5000 | 3216 | 4891 | 4891 | | 7777 | 6432 | 7705 | 7705 | | 12345 | 10720 | 12261 | 12261 | | 14999 | 12864 | 14874 | 14874 | `before` comes from a CPU replica driving the real splitter and the real managers on the base commit; on the patched build that replica reproduces the end-to-end numbers length by length, so the two columns are comparable. Configurations where the patch must be inert: re-running the same 132 lengths without `--prefix-match-unit` (both groups sit at 1072, so `hash_block_size == block_size` and sub-page hashing is off) gives `((P - 1) // 1072) * 1072 - 1072` on every length, and the CPU replica shows this build and the base commit agreeing on all 132. `mamba_cache_mode=all` cannot be exercised on this model — it is not in `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching`, so vLLM falls back to `align`. Unit tests: `tests/v1/core` 492 passed. The one failure and two errors are GPU-exclusive e2e cases (`Free memory on device cuda:0 ... less than desired`) blocked by the serving process on the same box, and reproduce without this change. `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` is updated so the replay landing position counts as a legal intermediate chunk end alongside the partial-tail boundary. signals.title: [Bugfix][Anthropic] Return 4xx for client-caused errors in /v1/messages
signals.text: ## Purpose Closes #52088. Invalid user input that passes the Anthropic request schema but fails the Anthropic→OpenAI conversion (e.g. more than `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS` stop sequences) currently surfaces as an **HTTP 500**: the `except Exception` in `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` swallows the `pydantic.ValidationError` raised while constructing `ChatCompletionRequest` and turns it into an `internal_error`. The schema half of #52088 was already addressed by #51997 (`max_length` on `stop_sequences`, so `/openapi.json` advertises `maxItems: 4`). This PR fixes the remaining robustness gap: client-caused errors must be **4xx**, never 500. ## Changes - `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` - Added `_translate_exception()` helper shared by both routes. - `pydantic.ValidationError` (a `ValueError` subclass) and `VLLMClientError` raised by the serving/conversion layer now map to **400 Bad Request** via the existing `create_error_response` + `translate_error_response` helpers. - Genuine server errors keep the existing 500 `internal_error` behaviour. - Applies to both `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`. - `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` - New `TestClientErrorResponses` class: conversion `ValidationError` → 400, `VLLMValidationError` → 400, generic `RuntimeError` → 500 (regression guard), and the `count_tokens` route → 400. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestClientErrorResponses python -m ruff check vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py python -m ruff format --check vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py ``` ## Test Result - `py_compile` + `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`: clean. - Error-mapping behaviour verified against a real `pydantic.ValidationError` (6 stop sequences): maps to `BadRequestError` / 400; `VLLMClientError` → 400; `RuntimeError` → 500. - Full unit tests run in CI (local environment cannot import the vLLM C extension, so the pytest suite is executed on Buildkite). --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [AMD] [Rocm]Enable DCP support in vLLM for the A2A communication path
signals.text: ## Summary - Enable the ROCm AITER MLA decode backend to participate in decode context parallelism (DCP), including the A2A communication path. - Size persistent decode metadata for the DCP-gathered query-head count instead of the local TP shard count. For Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 this changes the decode view from 12 local heads to 96 gathered heads. - Return AITER decode log-sum-exp (LSE) values so vLLM can combine partial attention outputs across KV shards, and remove any AITER head padding from both output and LSE tensors. - Preserve the existing non-DCP AITER wrapper path. ROCm AITER DCP currently supports single-token decode; multi-token verification is rejected until global CPRR metadata is supported. ## Environment ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export AITER_DISABLE_FMHA_OPUS=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 export HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200 export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0 export VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE=0 ``` ## vLLM serve command Use `ROCM_AITER_MLA` explicitly to exercise the code changed by this PR: ```bash vllm serve /mnt/disk_nvme1n1/huggingface/hub/kimik3 \ --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --language-model-only \ --moe-backend auto \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \ --dcp-comm-backend a2a \ --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \ --load-format fastsafetensors \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --max-model-len auto \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":16,"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' ``` ## Code changes - `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` derives the effective decode head count from `num_heads * dcp_world_size` and uses it for Gluon routing and persistent metadata generation. - `AiterMLAImpl` advertises decode-LSE support and validates the DCP-gathered query shape. - The DCP path calls AITER's native `mla_decode_fwd(..., return_lse=True)` because the vLLM custom-op wrapper discards LSE. - Output and LSE tensors are unpadded consistently before vLLM performs its cross-rank LSE-weighted reduction. - Non-DCP execution continues through `rocm_aiter_ops.mla_decode_fwd` unchanged. ## Benchmark Configuration: - Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` - Hardware: 8 ROCm GPUs - A2A case: TP8/DCP8, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` - Baseline case: TP8 without DCP - Input/output length: 512,000 / 1,024 tokens per request - Measured prompts: 10 after 3 warmups - Maximum concurrency: 8 - Both cases completed 10/10 requests with zero failures on the successful paired attempt. | Metric | DCP8 A2A | TP8 baseline | A2A difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 5,294.06 tok/s | 3,843.90 tok/s | +37.7% | | Request throughput | 0.01032 req/s | 0.00749 req/s | +37.7% | | Benchmark duration | 969.06 s | 1,334.65 s | -27.4% | | Mean TTFT | 216.7 s | 539.9 s | -59.9% | | Mean TPOT | 442.8 ms | 204.1 ms | +116.9% | A2A improved aggregate throughput by 37.7% and reduced total workload duration by 27.4%. It substantially reduced time to first token, while the TP8 baseline retained lower per-output-token latency. ## Accuracy Test Result #### GSM8K python3 tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py\ --num-questions 1319 \ --num-shots 5 \ --max-tokens 256 \ --host http://127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --temperature 0 \ --seed 42 \ --max-concurrency 8 \ --save-results \ /bench/gsm8k-aiter-a2a-20260814T025014Z-retry.json #### Result <html> <body> <!--StartFragment--> Tasks | Version | Filter | n-shot | Metric | | Value | | Stderr -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- gsm8k | vLLM | flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match | ↑ | 0.9447 | ± | 0.0063 <!--EndFragment--> </body> </html> ## Test plan - [x] `git diff --check` - [x] Static diagnostics for the modified backend - [x] DCP8 A2A benchmark: 10/10 requests completed - [x] TP8 baseline benchmark: 10/10 requests completed - [ ] Run focused Python unit tests (pytest is not installed in the current checkout environment)

signals.title: [Metrics] Add operation label to Prometheus latency histograms
signals.text: ## Problem The [OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-metrics.md) require `gen_ai.operation.name` as a **Required** attribute on server-side metrics like `gen_ai.server.request.duration`. vLLM's Prometheus latency histograms currently have no way to distinguish between chat, completion, and embedding operations — making it impossible for an OTel Collector to produce spec-compliant `gen_ai.*` metrics via label remapping. ## Related work (none adds the `operation` label to Prometheus metrics) - #20372 — V1 engine tracing (spans only, not metrics). - #35469 — OTel Metrics via OTLP push, but mirrors existing labels without adding `operation`. - #31162 — OTel tracing for startup/loading phase, unrelated to request metrics. ## Solution Add an `operation` label to latency histograms at the source. The entrypoints set the value (`chat`, `text_completion`, `embeddings`), and it flows through the engine to the Prometheus stat logger. ## Test plan **Unit tests:** ```bash pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py -v # 2 passed ``` **Integration test (Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on GPU):** ```bash curl -s http://localhost:8192/metrics | grep 'operation=' ``` ``` vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket{...operation="chat",...} 1.0 vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket{...operation="text_completion",...} 1.0 ``` **OTel Collector pipeline test (local, no Kubernetes):** ``` gen_ai.server.request.duration{gen_ai.operation.name="chat", gen_ai.request.model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", gen_ai.system="vllm"} ```

signals.title: [CI] Increase extended generation test timeout
signals.text: ## Summary Raise the **Language Models Test (Extended Generation)** timeout from 65 to 80 minutes. This keeps the existing test coverage and single-H200 resource shape unchanged. ## Why PR #48186 reduced this timeout from 110 to 65 minutes based on one successful 48.9-minute nightly and a 15-minute buffer. Runtime variance has since consumed that buffer: - [main #78476](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/78476/canvas?jid=019f6cbb-c4f5-45f7-861d-bac2659246a8&tab=output) passed in 64m57s. - Main timed out on July 17, July 20, July 22, and [August 13](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/83797/canvas?jid=019ffced-fea8-4b35-8325-f34f24f8a27b&tab=output). - The [August 13 retry](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/83797/canvas?jid=019ffd60-4fb5-432d-8261-55c99025a4a1&tab=output) passed in about 52 minutes. An 80-minute ceiling restores roughly 15 minutes of headroom above the observed near-65-minute runs. It avoids consuming a second H200 for sharding and does not remove or narrow any tests. ## Duplicate work No open issue or pull request was found for this timeout adjustment. PR #48186 is related historical context, but it introduced the 65-minute value rather than fixing the resulting timeouts. ## Validation - `yq eval '.' .buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml` - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml` - `git diff --check` All applicable checks passed. An H200 test run was not performed locally because this is a Buildkite timeout-only change. ## Model evaluation Not applicable. This changes only CI timeout metadata and does not affect model behavior, output, or accuracy. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to trace the main-branch timeout history, identify the regression in PR #48186, prepare the change, and draft this description. signals.title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V4: don't emit an empty `<think></think>` block for reasoningless turns
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52253. `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4_encoding.py` rendered an assistant turn carrying no `reasoning` as a literal empty thinking block, `<｜Assistant｜><think></think>`. Declaring tools force-disables `drop_thinking`: ```python if any(m.get("tools") for m in full_messages): effective_drop_thinking = False ``` so every prior assistant turn keeps its thinking block — but when the client does not echo `reasoning` back for a turn, there is nothing to put in it. `<think></think>` appears in **none** of the four expected outputs shipped with the checkpoint. Wherever those fixtures have an assistant turn whose reasoning is not rendered, the encoding is chat-style — `</think>` placed directly after `<｜Assistant｜>`: - [`encoding/tests/test_output_2.txt`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/blob/main/encoding/tests/test_output_2.txt) begins `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>You are a helpful assistant.<｜User｜>Hello<｜Assistant｜></think>Hi there! ...`, and [`test_encoding_dsv4.py`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/blob/main/encoding/test_encoding_dsv4.py) asserts `encode_messages(messages, thinking_mode="thinking") == gold` for it. - The reference encoder's own `drop_thinking` path emits the same form for turns before the last user message. - [`encoding/README.md`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/blob/main/encoding/README.md) documents `</think>` placed right after `<｜Assistant｜>` to close the block immediately. So the reference encoding has two spellings for one situation — "thinking mode, assistant turn whose reasoning is not rendered". The `drop_thinking` spelling is attested and asserted; the tools spelling is neither, and no fixture covers `tools present + reasoning absent`. ## Changes Introduce `opens_thinking_block()`, a single predicate shared by the transition branch and the assistant branch, so the two cannot disagree about whether a block was opened. A turn whose reasoning will not be rendered is encoded chat-style. The assistant branch only closes a block the preceding user/developer message actually opened, so behaviour is unchanged when no transition ran. Explicitly preserved: - turns that carry reasoning are byte-identical to before - the generation prompt still ends `<｜Assistant｜><think>` so the model can reason - `chat` mode, `drop_thinking`, and the `task` marker paths are untouched ## Test Plan New parametrized tests in `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py` cover `reasoning=""` and a missing `reasoning` key, asserting no `<think></think>`, the chat-style form present, and the generation prompt intact — plus a test that a reasoning-carrying turn is unchanged. ## Test Result Rendering all four reference fixtures with this change is **byte-identical to `main`**, and all four still match the expected outputs: ``` case 1 (thinking): PATCHED==gold True | patched==upstream True case 2 (thinking): PATCHED==gold True | patched==upstream True case 3 (thinking): PATCHED==gold True | patched==upstream True case 4 (chat ): PATCHED==gold True | patched==upstream True ``` The new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change: ``` upstream reasoning="" | "<think></think>" present: True upstream reasoning=missing | "<think></think>" present: True patched reasoning="" | "<think></think>" present: False patched reasoning=missing | "<think></think>" present: False ``` Observed effect on a real deployment: in a ~336k-token tool-calling conversation containing 104 such blocks (the last 17 assistant turns consecutive), the model emitted `</think>` as its first generated token and produced no reasoning on every sample. Encoding only those turns chat-style restored reasoning. Downstream quality degradation had additional contributing factors and is not claimed here.
signals.author: flexwang

signals.title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V4: render request-level tools after the system prompt
signals.text: ## Purpose `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` inserted a **new** empty system message to carry request-level tools rather than attaching them to the existing one: ```python if tools is not None and len(tools) > 0: messages.insert(0, {"role": "system"}) messages[0]["tools"] = tools ``` The empty message renders as `""` + `"\n\n"` + the tools block, so the entire `## Tools` section lands **before** the system prompt. For a 53-tool schema that moves ~25k tokens, and the prompt diverges from the reference encoding at **token 6** — which is also the prefix-cache root. ### Why after the system prompt is correct The reference implementation shipped with the checkpoint attaches tools to the existing message. [`encoding/test_encoding_dsv4.py`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/blob/main/encoding/test_encoding_dsv4.py) does ```python messages[0]["tools"] = td["tools"] prompt = encode_messages(messages, thinking_mode="thinking") assert prompt == gold ``` and [`encoding/tests/test_output_1.txt`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/blob/main/encoding/tests/test_output_1.txt) begins: ``` <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>You are a helpful assistant. ## Tools ``` Rendering case 1 both ways against that golden: ``` tools attached to the existing system message : == gold True tools in a newly inserted system message : == gold False ``` ### Why CI did not catch it `tests/tokenizers_/fixtures/deepseek_v4/test_output_1.txt` had been regenerated to match the inserted-message layout, so `test_deepseek_v4_matches_reference_golden_fixtures[1]` was asserting the wrong output: | | md5 | |---|---| | checkpoint original | `c40a74c9492a3d0d1e8b2d50d140ac56` | | vendored in-tree (before this PR) | `596044c041eda7f8fb55e2ee39cf725d` | Cases 2, 3 and 4 were already byte-identical to the checkpoint and are untouched. Case 1 is the only tools case, which is exactly why it was the only one that drifted. ## Changes - Attach request-level tools to the leading `system`/`developer` message; insert one only when there is nothing to attach to. - Restore `test_output_1.txt` from the checkpoint, so the existing golden test enforces the reference layout. - `developer` is included because the reference renders tools for that role too. - Request-level tools now **replace** tools already present on that message. Previously both were rendered, emitting the `## Tools` block twice. ## Test Plan The existing parametrized `test_deepseek_v4_matches_reference_golden_fixtures` becomes the regression test once the fixture is restored — it fails on `main` for case 1 and passes with this change. Four new tests cover: tools after a system prompt, tools after a `developer` prompt, insertion when no system/developer message exists, and request-level tools replacing message-level ones. ## Test Result All four restored goldens, rendered through the wrapper's marshalling: ``` case upstream==gold PATCHED==gold 1 False True 2 True True 3 True True 4 True True ``` Case 3 is unaffected because its tools arrive on a `developer` message rather than at request level, so the insert branch never fires there. Edge cases, before → after: ``` developer-first, request-level tools : tools-first -> developer-first, 1 tools block no system/developer message : 1 tools block -> 1 tools block (unchanged) message already carries tools : 2 tools blocks -> 1 tools block (request-level wins) ``` ## Note for reviewers This changes the rendered prompt for every DeepSeek-V4 request that passes tools at request level, so it invalidates existing prefix caches and can shift eval numbers. The restored golden is the justification: the new layout is the checkpoint's own expected output, not a preference. I could not determine why the in-tree fixture was changed. If that was deliberate rather than a red test being regenerated, I'd rather hear it before this lands.

signals.title: [Quantization] Support per-block FP8 for Quark fused MoE layers
signals.text: ## Purpose `QuarkConfig._is_fp8_w8a8` already accepts per-block (128x128) FP8 weights, and #47972 added `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` so that **linear** layers can consume them. `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` was never updated, so it still rejects the `per_block` qscheme: ``` ValueError: For FP8 Fused MoE layers, only per-tensor and per-channel scales for weights and activations are supported. Found per_block, per_group ``` The result is an asymmetry: for a Quark checkpoint whose routed experts are quantized per-block, every linear layer loads fine but the MoE layers cannot be built at all. ### Concrete case: the MTP layer of an MoE model Models that ship an MTP (multi-token prediction) draft layer make this asymmetry easy to see, because vLLM builds the MTP layer from the *same* decoder-layer class as the main model. For `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B`, `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor` instantiates `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(layer_type="full_attention")`, which for an MoE config contains a complete `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` with all 512 routed experts. Broken down by quantization path (`{i}` runs over `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, default 1): | Module | vLLM layer | Quant path | Status | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `mtp.embed_tokens` | `VocabParallelEmbedding` | — | not quantized | | `mtp.fc` | `ColumnParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.norm`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_hidden`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding` | `Qwen3_5RMSNorm` | — | not quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.self_attn.qkv_proj` | `QKVParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.self_attn.o_proj` | `RowParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.gate` | `ReplicatedLinear`, built with `quant_config=None` | — | never quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert_gate` | `ReplicatedLinear`, built with `quant_config=None` | — | never quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert.gate_up_proj` | `MergedColumnParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert.down_proj` | `RowParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | **`mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.experts`** | **`RoutedExperts`** | **fused MoE** | **rejected — fixed by this PR** | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.experts` is the only module in the MTP stack that takes the fused-MoE path, and it is the only one that fails. It is also not a small module: with `hidden_size=4096`, `moe_intermediate_size=1024` and 512 experts it holds roughly 6.4B parameters, so leaving it unquantized is not a practical workaround. Two related details worth noting: - `mlp.gate` and `mlp.shared_expert_gate` are constructed with a hardcoded `quant_config=None`, so they are never quantized regardless of the Quark config. - When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` is enabled and the shared expert is not excluded from quantization, `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` sets `shared_expert = None` and folds the shared expert into the routed-expert tensors, which moves those weights onto the fused-MoE path as well. ## Changes All changes are inside the existing `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`, following the `BLOCK` strategy of `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` rather than adding a new class: the weight, bias, input-scale and kernel-setup code is shared with the per-tensor and per-channel paths, and only the scale layout, the scale parameter name and a few flags differ. - `__init__`: accept `per_block`; read `block_size` from the weight config; use `kFp8Static128BlockSym` / `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` for backend selection; require dynamic activation quantization for per-block weights; select the scale parameter name (`weight_scale_inv` for per-block, `weight_scale` otherwise) the way `Fp8MoEMethod` already does. - `create_weights`: propagate `layer.weight_block_size`; validate that `intermediate_size_per_partition` is divisible by `block_n` (and by `block_k` when TP > 1) so misalignment fails at weight-creation time rather than silently producing wrong results in the kernel; allocate block-grid weight scales, register them as `w13_weight_scale_inv` / `w2_weight_scale_inv`, and tag them with `FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported.BLOCK` so `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` shards them on the block grid instead of per row. - `process_weights_after_loading`, `_setup_kernel` and `get_fused_moe_quant_config`: look the weight scales up through the selected name, and pass `block_shape` through to `make_fp8_moe_quant_config`. The per-tensor requantization loop and the per-channel `unsqueeze` in `process_weights_after_loading` remain guarded on `weight_qscheme`, and per-block weights require dynamic activations so the static input-scale branch is skipped. The only per-block change there is routing the fnuz normalization through the selected scale name, so per-block also works on MI300. The per-tensor and per-channel paths are unchanged: `block_shape` stays `None`, the scale parameters keep the `weight_scale` name, and the scale shapes are identical to before. ### Why the per-block scales are named `weight_scale_inv` Block-quantized checkpoints store their per-block scales as `weight_scale_inv` (the deepseek-v3 convention Quark follows), and `RoutedExperts.load_weights` derives the parameter name from the checkpoint tensor name by replacing only the module-path portion and carrying the suffix over verbatim — `...experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv` resolves to `w2_weight_scale_inv`, with no aliasing step in between. Registering the scales under `w2_weight_scale` therefore made every per-block checkpoint fail to load: ``` AttributeError: Layer mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts has no parameter 'w2_weight_scale_inv' for checkpoint weight 'mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv' ``` Both names hold the same quantity (a dequantization multiplier, multiplied into the block-scaled GEMM), so this is purely a lookup-key mismatch and it always fails loudly. ## Test Plan Added to `tests/quantization/test_quark.py`: - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_requires_block_size` — a per-block weight config without `block_size` is rejected. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_rejects_per_block_static_input` — static activations are rejected for per-block weights. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_weight_shapes` — `w13`/`w2` weight and scale shapes, that the scales are registered under the `weight_scale_inv` name and not under `weight_scale`, and that both scales carry the `BLOCK` loader attribute. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_rejects_misaligned_partition` — a partition size that is not a multiple of `block_n` fails during `create_weights`. ```bash pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block ``` ## Test Result Hardware: 1x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm. Checkpoint: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` re-quantized with AMD Quark from `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` into an NVFP4 backbone plus a per-block FP8 MTP layer (775 MTP modules per-block FP8, 10 kept in BF16 through `exclude`). This reproduces the asymmetry described above: the MTP `mlp.experts` module is per-block FP8 while the main model is NVFP4. ### Load and module routing TP=1, `speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}`: | Model | Module | Bound method | | --- | --- | --- | | target | 40 MoE layers | `QuarkNvfp4MoEMethod` | | drafter (MTP) | `mlp.experts.routed_experts` | `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` | | drafter (MTP) | `self_attn.qkv_proj`, `self_attn.o_proj`, `shared_expert.{gate_up,down}_proj` | `QuarkLinearMethod` / `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` | | drafter (MTP) | `fc`, `mlp.gate`, `mlp.shared_expert_gate` | `UnquantizedLinearMethod` | Backends selected, with no fallbacks reported: ``` Selected TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel for QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock Using TRITON Fp8 MoE backend Using 'EMULATION' NvFp4 MoE backend ``` ### MTP acceptance `Draft acceptance rate: 94.7%-95.9%`, acceptance length 1.96 out of a maximum of 2 for `num_speculative_tokens=1`. This is the most direct evidence that the per-block expert weights and scales are loaded correctly: a scale mismatch drives acceptance towards 0. ### GSM8K `lm_eval` 5-shot over the full 1319 questions, chat template with thinking disabled: | Filter | exact_match | | --- | --- | | flexible-extract | 0.9629 ± 0.0052 | | strict-match | 0.9636 ± 0.0052 | ```bash lm_eval --model vllm \ --model_args pretrained=<ckpt>,max_model_len=262144,gpu_memory_utilization=0.45,max_gen_toks=2048,trust_remote_code=True,enable_thinking=False \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto \ --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn ``` A note for anyone reproducing this with the plain completion-style `gsm8k` task: the same checkpoint scores only ~0.76 there, and that gap is a harness artifact rather than a quantization effect. Qwen3.5 enters thinking mode non-deterministically on raw few-shot prompts (37% of samples in one run); those samples score 0.422 while the non-thinking samples score 0.951, and most of the thinking failures stop early because the model writes a `... Question:` heading that collides with the task's `until: ["Question:"]` stop string. Two identical completion-mode runs differed by 2 points for the same reason. ### Unit tests ``` pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block 8 passed, 35 deselected ``` This covers the four new MoE tests above together with the pre-existing per-block linear tests from #47972, which still pass.

signals.title: [CI][AMD] Improve Kubernetes failure diagnostics
signals.text: AMD CI failures currently flood the Buildkite log with host-oriented diagnostics and can leave native or single-node Docker work behind after timeouts and signals. This change keeps the terminal summary short, uploads pod-aware diagnostics as a Buildkite artifact, and selectively incorporates the durable teardown logic. The diagnostics and teardown now share one failure path so cleanup cannot suppress the artifact or alter the original test status. - Capture cgroup v1/v2 CPU, memory, OOM, pressure, PID, I/O, process, mount, `/dev/shm`, GPU, and network evidence in `artifacts/amd-ci-failure-diagnostics/.../diagnostics.log`. - Keep failure output to a three-line summary, preserve the original exit status, and retain non-GPU diagnostics for CPU-only jobs. - Track native and single-node Docker tests in dedicated process groups, enforce the remaining CI timeout, terminate escaped tagged descendants, and clean only job-labeled containers with bounded Docker commands.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Preserve engine content without tool calls
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52214. When an engine-backed tool parser is used without a reasoning parser, the non-streaming no-tool-call path currently discards the parser engine's normalized content and returns the original model output. This can leak format markers such as Inkling content-block delimiters into the API response. Return `tool_call_info.content` only for engine-based parser compositions when automatic parsing finds no tool call. Plain tool parsers keep the existing behavior of returning the untouched input. The regression coverage verifies both sides of that boundary: - an engine-backed, tool-only Inkling parser returns clean plain-text content when no tool is called; - a non-engine tool parser still returns the original input even if its no-call result contains transformed content. ### Duplicate-work check I searched open pull requests for #52214 and for DelegatingParser engine/no-tool-call content handling. No open PR addresses this issue. Nearby PRs concern token-ID preservation, streaming finalization, or `tool_choice="none"`, not this non-streaming no-call handoff. The issue reporter also confirmed that they are not preparing a patch and asked me to proceed. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py -q HF_HOME=/path/to/writable/cache .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/test_parse.py -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/path/to/writable/cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \\ vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py \\ tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py \\ tests/parser/test_parse.py ``` ## Test Result Before the production fix, the new Inkling regression fails with: ```text Expected: The answer is 42. Actual: <|content_text|>The answer is 42.<|end_message|> ``` With the fix: - focused parser tests: 106 passed; - full parser-engine suite: 3,784 passed; - all relevant pre-commit hooks passed; - `git diff --check` passed. ### Model evaluation Not run. This is a unit-level parser-composition fix that requires no model weights or GPU; the failure and corrected output are deterministically covered with the existing mock tokenizer and parser-engine tests. ### AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex was used to investigate, implement, test, and draft this pull request. I reviewed the changed lines and test results. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and linked issue are described. - [x] The test plan is provided. - [x] The before/after test results are provided. - [x] No documentation update is required because this corrects internal parser behavior without changing the public interface. </details>

signals.title: [ROCm] Give EngineCore cleanup grace after request abort
signals.text: AMD CI exposed a shutdown race where `shutdown_timeout=0` aborted requests as intended but also gave EngineCore no time to release ROCm resources before SIGKILL. This change preserves immediate request abort while giving the ROCm EngineCore process manager a bounded 60-second cleanup grace when both the configured and remaining process timeouts are zero. It keeps exhausted budgets for positive shutdown timeouts unchanged and extends the DP supervisor's outer deadline to cover the cleanup window. - The motivating failure is [AMD CI build 12007](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12007/list?sid=019ffc53-a1ab-472f-8b77-7c52a7d6edc0&tab=output). - The final request completed successfully, but EngineCore was force-killed immediately and GPU memory remained at 11.72 GB for the full 120-second release wait. - The `LLM()` to `vllm_runner()` migration does not cover this path because these tests launch a real out-of-process `vllm serve` server. - Add a ROCm-only 60-second EngineCore process cleanup grace when both the configured request timeout and remaining process timeout are zero. - Keep `shutdown_timeout=0` inside EngineCore so in-flight requests are still aborted immediately. - Preserve exhausted positive shutdown deadlines instead of accidentally granting them a fresh cleanup window. - Extend the DP supervisor's outer wait budget so it does not kill the process tree before EngineCore cleanup can finish. - Add manager and DP supervisor regression coverage in the existing test files.

signals.title: [CI] Harden RemoteVLLMServer GPU cleanup checks
signals.text: This PR is stacked on `akaratza_enginecore_shutdown` and hardens `RemoteVLLMServer` cleanup after a server exits. GPU baselines and cleanup waits are tracked per child-visible physical device, including overlapping multi-server scopes, so one leaked allocation cannot be hidden by a later aggregate baseline. Unavailable telemetry and timed-out cleanup now fail closed and retain affected-scope state until recovery can be verified. The test server's outer termination window also covers the EngineCore cleanup grace introduced by the first PR. - Prevent a teardown failure from ratcheting leaked VRAM into the next server's `_pre_server_gpu_memory` baseline. - Measure the physical devices selected by each child server's visibility environment on ROCm and CUDA. - Preserve parent-logical ordinal measurement on XPU, where `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` cannot consume physical or tile mask IDs. - Retain cleanup poison while intentionally concurrent servers make recovery unverifiable, and fail closed for unsafe partial coverage. - Merge partially overlapping scopes and use the earliest per-device baseline so a broader server cannot hide a leak behind an earlier sibling's allocation. - Keep GPU-less render-server tests outside GPU release accounting.

signals.title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Apply thinking budget to greedy requests
signals.text: ## Summary - Ensure Model Runner V2 does not take the no-logits-processing fast path when a scheduled request has an active thinking token budget. - Add focused GPU regression coverage for greedy sampling. ## Problem The Model Runner V2 sampler returns logits unchanged when `_requires_logits_processing()` is false. The predicate covered penalties, bad words, and non-default sampling, but did not cover `ThinkingBudgetState`. As a result, a greedy request with only `thinking_token_budget` enabled could bypass `apply_thinking_budget()` entirely. This made the budget ineffective even though the request state was configured correctly. This change includes active thinking-budget rows in the predicate. Requests without a thinking budget keep the existing fast path. ## Why this is not a duplicate The thinking-budget implementation was added in #46727, while the logits-processing fast path was introduced in #47711. This PR fixes the interaction between those changes. Immediately before submission, open-PR searches for `thinking_token_budget greedy` and `_requires_logits_processing` returned no matches. Broader sampler searches only returned speculative-decoding and frontend changes that do not modify this predicate. ## Tests - `uv run ruff check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py` - Passed - `uv run ruff format --check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py` - Passed - `uv run pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py` - Passed - `python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py -v` in the CUDA validation container - Baseline plus the new regression test: failed as expected because the end-reasoning logit remained `0.0` instead of `1.0e9` - Patched source: `13 passed` ## Model validation Validated on a task-owned GPU with ModelScope Qwen3.5-9B: - Greedy request without thinking returned the exact expected response. - Greedy request with `thinking_token_budget=5` stopped reasoning and produced the final answer successfully. - Existing service workloads on the other GPU were not modified. The GPU source-overlay baseline was `ac7509e2`. The submitted base is `8e6d8e4f`; the intervening upstream change only touches XPU/release files and does not overlap this sampler or test. Static checks were rerun on the submitted base. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation evidence and can defend the change end-to-end.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fall back when zentorch import fails
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52238. On AMD Zen CPU builds, a non-`ImportError` raised while importing zentorch currently escapes `cpu_platform_plugin`. Platform discovery then silently drops the CPU plugin and selects `UnspecifiedPlatform`. This change logs the underlying zentorch import failure and falls back to the standard `CpuPlatform`. A CPU-only regression test covers an incompatible shared library represented by `OSError`. I reviewed the issue comments and searched open PRs for both `#52238` and the zentorch CPU-platform import path. No overlapping open PR was found. AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. I reviewed every changed line of code and the regression test, and I understand and can defend the change end-to-end. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py -q .venv/bin/ruff check --ignore ISC004 vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py ``` The repository pre-commit hooks also ran during commit. ## Test Result - Before the implementation, the new regression test failed with the simulated `OSError: incompatible shared library` escaping platform detection. - After the implementation: `5 passed in 0.62s`. - Ruff check and format check passed. - All commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and repository policy checks. - An additional platform-plugin test was attempted with its required dummy plugin installed. Its platform assertion passed, but the process later segfaulted in the existing macOS PyTorch global cleanup path at `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache`; this is outside the changed code. - Model evaluations were not run because this change does not affect model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior. No documentation update is needed.

signals.title: [Model][Generative Recommendation] Add HSTU model support to vLLM
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR adds HSTU-based generative recommendation model support to vLLM. HSTU is a ranking model architecture designed for generative recommendation. Unlike traditional language models, HSTU does not autoregressively generate text tokens. Instead, it synchronously computes ranking scores for all candidate items in a request. The goal of this change is to enable generative recommendation models to reuse the existing vLLM and large-model serving ecosystem, including: - Hugging Face model and configuration loading. - vLLM model registration. - GPU model execution. - Attention backend selection. - Optimized CUDA operators. - Request batching and scheduling. - Asynchronous output handling. - CUDA Graph execution. - Future distributed inference and online serving infrastructure. Generative recommendation and large language models have several common characteristics. Both can be represented as sequence models, use embedding layers and transformer-style computation, and benefit from optimized attention kernels, GPU batching, asynchronous execution, and production-level model serving infrastructure. By integrating HSTU into vLLM, generative recommendation models can reuse the existing large-model ecosystem instead of maintaining an independent inference stack. ## Inference Paradigm Although HSTU and large language models share several model and runtime components, their inference semantics are different. | Aspect | Large language model | Generative recommendation model | | --- | --- | --- | | Decode behavior | Autoregressively generates one token at a time | Synchronously computes scores for all candidates in a request | | Model output | Vocabulary logits for the next token | One ranking score for each candidate item | | Sampling | Requires token sampling and token ID generation | Does not generate a sampled token | | Request progress | Continues until the requested number of tokens is generated | Completes after all candidate scores are returned | | Output format | Usually `[num_tokens, vocab_size]` | Packed candidate-score output | | Scheduler signal | Uses sampled token IDs to update request state | Uses candidate scores to complete the request | The default vLLM generation path is designed around language-model execution: 1. Run the model forward pass. 2. Produce vocabulary logits. 3. Invoke the token sampler. 4. Generate token IDs. 5. Update the request state. 6. Continue decoding until the request is finished. This flow cannot be directly reused for HSTU because HSTU produces candidate ranking scores rather than vocabulary logits. Passing HSTU outputs through the normal sampler would incorrectly interpret candidate scores as vocabulary logits and could produce invalid token IDs. Therefore, this PR adds a score-only execution path: 1. Run the HSTU forward pass. 2. Extract the score corresponding to each candidate item. 3. Convert candidate IDs and scores into `LogprobsTensors`. 4. Return the scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. 5. Skip the standard token sampler. 6. Skip generated-token state updates. 7. Complete the request after all candidate scores are returned. The scheduler is also updated to support score-only recommendation requests. A request can be completed after candidate scores are produced even when no `new_token_ids` are returned. ## Implementation Overview This PR contains five main categories of changes. ### 1. Model Structure and Model Registration Files: - `vllm/model_executor/models/hstu.py` - `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` - `tests/models/registry.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU model implementation. - Add HSTU embedding layers, transformer blocks, normalization layers, and prediction heads. - Register the HSTU model with vLLM. - Support Hugging Face HSTU model loading. - Add HSTU to the model registry test data. - Add model registration and model import coverage. ### 2. Model Configuration and Configuration Registration Files: - `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/hstu.py` Changes: - Add HSTU-specific configuration classes. - Support HSTU model and task configuration fields. - Support `model_type = "hstu"`. - Convert HSTU configuration data from Hugging Face configuration files into the vLLM configuration representation. - Preserve compatibility with the existing vLLM configuration loading flow. ### 3. Model Operators and Operator Registration Files: - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/hstu_attn.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU attention backend. - Integrate the external HSTU variable-length attention operator. - Register the HSTU attention backend with vLLM. - Automatically select `HSTU_ATTN` for HSTU or generative recommendation models when no explicit backend is configured. - Preserve explicit attention backend configuration as the highest-priority option. - Validate unsupported attention combinations and return clear errors. - Pass per-request context and candidate metadata to the HSTU attention implementation. Automatic backend selection is only applied when the user has not explicitly selected an attention backend. This preserves the existing backend override behavior. ### 4. Model Runner V1 Adaptation File: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` Changes: - Add generative recommendation metadata collection. - Add HSTU candidate score extraction. - Pass HSTU metadata through the forward context. - Bypass the standard token sampler for HSTU requests. - Return candidate scores through the prompt-logprobs output path. - Add recommendation-specific request completion handling. - Preserve the existing execution path for non-HSTU models. ### 5. Model Runner V2 Adaptation Files: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/gr_state.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py` - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` Changes: - Add `GRState` for request-scoped generative recommendation state. - Store user IDs, candidate count, prompt token IDs, and request stage. - Move candidate score extraction from the Model Runner into `GRState`. - Convert packed HSTU outputs into `LogprobsTensors`. - Add asynchronous score output handling. - Return candidate scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. - Skip token sampling and token-state updates for HSTU requests. - Complete score-only requests in the scheduler when candidate scores are available. - Preserve the one-token early-return behavior required by generative recommendation inputs. ## Test Plan ### 1. Environment Setup The operator is installed inside the following NVIDIA PyTorch container:`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.06-py3` Install the required system dependency:`apt update && apt install -y libxcb1` ### 2.HSTU Operator Installation and Validation The HSTU attention operator is provided by the NVIDIA `recsys-examples` repository. Clone the recsys-examples repository:`git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/recsys-examples.git && cd recsys-examples/corelib/hstu` For H20 and other Hopper-based devices, enter the corresponding device directory before compiling: `cd hopper` Install the HSTU operator:`Install the HSTU operator:` After the compilation completes successfully, validate the operator installation with: `python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu_op.py` ### 3.vLLM Installation Clone the vLLM repository:`git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git && cd vllm` Install the current vLLM source with CUDA support:`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda pip install -v -e .` ### 4. HSTU Model Inference: After the HSTU changes are included in vLLM, run:`python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu.py` This test validates: * HSTU model loading. * HSTU configuration loading. * HSTU model registration. * HSTU attention backend initialization. * HSTU forward execution. * Candidate score extraction. * Candidate ID and score formatting. * Score-only execution without token sampling. * Recommendation request completion. * Model Runner integration. * CUDA Graph execution. ### 5. Model Registry and Hugging Face Loading Run the model registry tests:`pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py -k HSTUForCausalLM` This validates that: * HSTUForCausalLM is registered. * The HSTU model class can be imported. * Hugging Face model metadata is available. * The HSTU configuration can be loaded. * The vLLM model registry can resolve the HSTU model. ## Test Result ### HSTU Operator The test returned like: ```text Input q shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Output shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Run success ``` ### HSTU Model Inference The test returned candidate IDs and their corresponding ranking scores. A truncated example of the output is: ```text Request 0: 12676:0.6602 47052:0.5078 45082:0.4336 79131:0.3984 34671:0.4844 5695:0.4570 95647:0.1777 60217:0.5273 70284:0.4258 16361:0.4238 Request 1: 8023:0.4863 24460:0.6094 ... ``` Each line follows the format:`Each line follows the format:` The output confirms that HSTU synchronously computes the scores of all candidates for a request and returns the scores through the generative recommendation output path. The test also confirms that: * HSTU outputs are not passed through the standard vocabulary sampler. * No artificial generated token IDs are produced. * Requests complete after candidate scores are returned. * Candidate scores are returned through prompt_logprobs_dict. * Both Model Runner V1 and Model Runner V2 execution paths are supported. * The HSTU attention backend is initialized and executed successfully. * CUDA Graph execution works in the validated CUDA environment. ### Model Registration and Hugging Face Loading The model registration and Hugging Face loading tests passed. HSTUForCausalLM can be resolved and imported through the vLLM model registry, and the HSTU configuration can be loaded from the Hugging Face model configuration. ### Scheduler and Score-Only Execution The scheduler validation passed for score-only recommendation requests. A recommendation request is correctly completed after candidate scores are produced, even when no new_token_ids are returned. The standard token sampling path is skipped for HSTU requests, and no regular language-model token state update is performed. ### Attention Backend Selection When no explicit attention backend is configured, the HSTU model automatically selects HSTU_ATTN. When an explicit attention backend is configured, the user-provided backend remains authoritative and is not overridden by the HSTU automatic selection logic. ### Current Scope and Limitations This initial integration focuses on bringing HSTU into the vLLM model and serving ecosystem. The current implementation assumes: * Prompt lengths are consistent across users. * Candidate lengths are consistent across users. * HSTU and non-HSTU requests are not mixed in the same batch. * Candidate scores are produced during an unchunked prefill. * Pipeline parallelism is not used. * PD-separated HSTU execution is not supported yet. * KV-cache-based or paged HSTU attention is not supported yet. * request_stage = 1 is not supported. * Each recommendation prompt contains at least one context/candidate pair. These limitations can be addressed in follow-up work after the basic HSTU execution path and serving interface are established.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Preserve SWA replay windows after EAGLE tail pop
signals.text: Fixes #51761 ## Purpose Preserve the sliding-window KV chunks needed when an EAGLE/MTP volatile-tail pop moves the shared replay boundary inside a full-attention alignment segment. The scheduler now derives the replay boundaries from the fixed prompt extent before the first store. It retains only the missing SWA windows as their chunks first become storable, including intermediate boundaries and the EAGLE peek chunk. Decode stores remain monotonic and do not scan below the existing store cursor. ## Test Plan - Exercise 30,208-, 30,272-, and 30,336-token prompt geometries through scheduler store jobs, real CPU offload completion, and an independent replay. - Split prompt storage into two batches with the first batch crossing the replay boundary, then verify a 64-token decode stores only its new SWA tail. - Cover both sliding-window and full-attention EAGLE groups. - Run focused formatting and lint checks on the changed files. ## Test Result - 30,208-token replay restores 30,144 tokens, with the two required C4 keys resident. - The aligned 30,272-token control restores 30,208 tokens with no supplemental keys. - The 30,336-token controls account for full-attention tightening and both EAGLE attention forms. - Focused regression: 4 passed. - Ruff format, Ruff lint, and diff whitespace checks passed. - The broader `TestEagle` class could not be validated in this local CPU snapshot because its request-runner cases are rejected during platform configuration, before their test logic executes. --- - [x] Purpose and linked issue considered. - [x] Test plan provided. - [x] Test results provided. - [x] Documentation impact considered; no user-facing interface changed.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: inherit the target's attention backend when the speculative config names none
signals.text: ## Purpose `load_dspark_model` passes `backend=speculative_config.attention_backend` when building the draft's config. That field is `None` unless the user names a backend inside `--speculative-config`, and `None` re-runs backend auto-selection rather than meaning "same as target" — so an explicitly pinned target backend is silently discarded and the draft can pick a different attention class. On DeepSeek V4 with `--attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, the target builds `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention` (plain 512B KV row) while the draft falls back to `DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention`, whose `__init__` rewrites the shared `cache_config.cache_dtype` to `fp8_ds_mla`. The SWA cache is then allocated at 584B/token but still reshaped at `head_dim`, on every rank at first forward: ``` RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 64, 512]' is invalid for input of size 4176917504 vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py, in _fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert ``` `4176917504 = 111754 * 64 * 584`, the `fp8_ds_mla` geometry. Fall back to the target's backend when the speculative config names none; an explicit `attention_backend` still wins. ## Why this is not a duplicate - **#40611** (open) lets the draft *deliberately differ* from the target. This fixes the *fallback* when nothing is specified; the explicit override still wins. - **#51538** / **#51042** fix a different DSV4 + DSpark defect (`decode_swa_indices` width). Independent of this one and deliberately not included. Each masks the other, verified on one config (DSV4-Pro-0813, TP8 × 2 GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, DSpark k=7): | fixes | result | | --- | --- | | neither | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid (this bug) | | this PR | passes, then fails in #51538's path: `shape '[7, 128]'` invalid | | #51538 | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid again (this bug) | | both | engine initializes and serves | ## Test plan `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py` → **2 passed**. `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py` → all pass (incl. mypy, ruff). ## Model evaluation aime25, 4 epochs (n=120), temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95, thinking on, `max_tokens=150000`, DSV4-Pro-0813 on TP8 × 2 GB300, same tree throughout. DSpark rows need #51538 applied too, since both are required to start: | configuration | exact_match | pass@4 | errors | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec | 1.0000 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark | 0.9917 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark (n=360) | 0.9778 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec (n=360) | 0.9944 | 1.0 | 0 | Mean acceptance length 3.16 at full concurrency. The DSpark row's single miss is a `length` truncation on the one AIME problem that runs long in every configuration tested, with no repetition loop. No unfixed baseline: the configuration cannot start without this fix. ## AI assistance This work was produced with AI assistance. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, and the tests and evaluations above were executed on the hardware described.

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Isolate tiering shutdown failures
signals.text: # [Bugfix][KV Offload] Continue tier cleanup after shutdown failures ## Purpose `TieringOffloadingManager.shutdown()` tears down secondary tiers before the CPU primary tier. Previously, an ordinary exception from one secondary tier immediately aborted the loop, skipping all later secondary tiers and the primary tier. The primary tier owns the memoryview and `SharedOffloadRegion` cleanup for the scheduler-side mmap. This change makes normal shutdown follow the same best-effort resource-ownership policy already used for tiering initialization cleanup: every secondary tier is attempted in configuration order, then the primary tier is attempted regardless of earlier ordinary exceptions. Failures remain observable through `logger.exception`, including the secondary tier index, configured tier type, and implementation class. The change intentionally does not catch `BaseException`, retry shutdown calls, or change scheduler and backend behavior. This reduces the graceful-shutdown risk that a secondary teardown exception prevents the primary mmap owner from releasing its resources. It does not address `SIGKILL`, process crashes, or a shutdown call that blocks forever. The most relevant in-tree failure surface is P2P teardown, which releases NIXL and ZMQ resources and can surface ordinary backend exceptions. The same is true for externally configured secondary tiers. File-system and object tiers handle most cleanup errors internally; a blocked lookup or I/O thread is a hang rather than an exception and is outside this change's scope. ## Why this is not a duplicate The duplicate-work search found no open PR that implements per-secondary-tier failure isolation in `TieringOffloadingManager.shutdown()`. This is distinct from #51622, which centralizes cleanup ordering for the CPU worker's GPU-to-CPU and CPU-to-GPU handlers. This change covers the scheduler-side tiering manager and ensures secondary-tier failure cannot skip the primary tier's mmap cleanup. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m compileall -q \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py \ PR_DESCRIPTION.md git diff --check ``` ## Test Result - `compileall`: passed. - `pre-commit`: all applicable hooks passed. - `git diff --check`: passed. - Model evaluation: not applicable; this only changes shutdown cleanup control flow. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used for repository inspection, implementation, and this PR description. The human submitter must review every changed line and run the validation they consider appropriate before submitting.
signals.author: Alex-ai-future

signals.title: [Bugfix] Add opt-out for synchronized FlashInfer autotune (multi-node deadlock without GPUDirect RDMA)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52291. Since the FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3 bump (#50892) wired `set_autotune_process_group` into `kernel_warmup.flashinfer_autotune` (design from #48714), multi-node startup deadlocks deterministically during autotuning on clusters whose inter-node transport is host-staged NCCL without GPUDirect RDMA (reproduced on 6× GB10 / DGX Spark class, TP=2 × PP=3): ranks desynchronize between tuning rounds, after which the cross-rank per-tactic timing collective blocks forever — one TP rank enters the next tuning round, its peer never does, both sit in futex wait at 0% GPU and startup never completes (full matrix in the issue: reproduced across FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3 / 0.6.17 / 0.6.18, pip and system NCCL, warm and cold JIT caches; the last pre-#50892 build tunes the identical workload cleanly every time). This PR adds `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DISTRIBUTED_SYNC` (default `1`, current behavior unchanged). Setting it to `0` restores the previous per-rank flow for distributed runs: every rank tunes independently, no autotune process group is set (so no cross-rank collectives run during tuning), and the persistent-cache broadcast is skipped because ranks may select different tactics. ## Test Plan - Deployed on the affected cluster (6× GB10, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, TP=2 × PP=3, vLLM `0.27.2rc1.dev54+gb96bcd0b4`, FlashInfer 0.6.18) with the opt-out active. - Compared against the same deployment with default settings, and with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=mxfp8_gemm`. ## Test Result - Default (synchronized): startup deadlocks in autotune every time (6/6 attempts across image/library permutations). - `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DISTRIBUTED_SYNC=0`: autotune completes on all ranks, startup succeeds, serving verified end-to-end; single-stream throughput 14.4–14.5 tok/s (vs 9.0 tok/s with the op skipped un-tuned) — matching the pre-#50892 baseline. - Single-node and default-path behavior unchanged (the new branch is only taken when `world_size > 1` and the env is explicitly disabled).
signals.author: Stupidoodle

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
signals.text: ## Purpose PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X): - **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build. - **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`. This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path. The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits. ## Changes - `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment). - `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`. - `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X. All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged. ## Performance The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step. ### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4) | Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% | | Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) | TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel. ### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us) Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel: | # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 | | 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | | | 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | | | 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | | | 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | | | 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | | | 7 | add | 4.45 | | | | 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | | | 9 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | | | 11 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | | | 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | | | 14 | mul | 4.33 | | | | 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | | | 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | | | | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** | ~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work). ## Not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"` ## Test Plan Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list: 1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`. 2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v` 3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k` 4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325` ## Test Result - Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance). - Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s - gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly. - `test_amd_kda_decode.py`: **12/12 passed** on MI325X (gfx942) — fused output matches the Triton reference across heads {12, 24, 96} x tokens {1, 7, 128}, plus the null-slot, no-output-norm, and padding edge cases. ## Checklist - [x] Compiles for gfx942 (kernel present in the .so with gfx942 codegen) - [x] `test_amd_kda_decode.py` passes on MI325X (12/12) - [x] gsm8k parity with the Triton path - [x] AI assistance used (see below) ## AI assistance This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). A human must review every line and run the build, tests, and eval on MI325X hardware before merge; the correctness and accuracy results above are not yet filled in.

signals.title: [bot] Enable google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant inference on Intel XPU
signals.text: ## Motivation `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant` uses the `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM` architecture and `gemma4_assistant` config type, which are not yet recognized by vLLM or the installed Transformers version. This PR adds the minimal plumbing to load and run this model. ## Technical Details 1. **Model registry**: Map `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM` → `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (same architecture, different config wrapper). 2. **Config classes**: Add `Gemma4AssistantConfig` and `Gemma4TextConfig` in `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/gemma4.py` so the checkpoint can be loaded without a Transformers upgrade. 3. **Config registry**: Register `gemma4_assistant` and `gemma4_text` model types. 4. **Model arch config convertor**: Register `gemma4_assistant` → `Gemma4ModelArchConfigConvertor`. 5. **KV shared layer fix**: Guard `first_kv_shared_layer_idx` with `> 0` to prevent false-positive shared-layer activation when the index is 0 (E2B has `num_kv_shared_layers=0`). 6. **Tokenizer fix**: Handle `extra_special_tokens` being a list instead of a dict (shipped by the gemma4_assistant tokenizer config), which causes an `AttributeError` in older Transformers. ## Testing - Model loads and generates correct output on Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60, Max 1550). - AI assistance was used (opencode agent). ## FYI This PR was generated with AI assistance.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Sync speculative draft tokens across PP ranks
signals.text: ## Purpose In Model Runner V2, speculative proposal runs only on the last pipeline rank. The resulting next-step draft tokens are written to that rank's request state, but the non-last ranks keep stale or zero-initialized draft tokens. Those ranks then reconstruct a different speculative verification input in the following PP step. This PR carries the next-step draft tokens together with the existing sampled-token PP broadcast and restores sampled and draft state together when the same delayed PP queue slot is consumed. It adds no collective and leaves non-PP paths unchanged. The transport is enabled for every speculative method that passes the existing MRV2 PP validation; unsupported methods still fail before `PPHandler` construction. This intentionally isolates only the draft-token synchronization issue from #46994. It does not include model enablement, model-specific projections, sparse-MLA backend changes, quantization, or weight-loading changes, so this correctness fix can be reviewed and merged independently. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ruff check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ruff format --check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ``` The corresponding MTP+PP path was also exercised with the vLLM Ascend backend using real-weight single-request inference and GSM8K evaluation. ## Test Result - Ruff check passed. - Ruff format check passed for all three changed files. - Targeted unit tests passed in the Ascend test container: `2 passed`. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing the test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Coordinate mmap host registration
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51762. Coordinate host registration across all TP x PCP x PP workers that map the same CPU KV-offload region. Workers now wait for a mapping fence, register in deterministic model-rank order, and make one group-wide decision from the registration results. If a normal registration call fails, every successful worker unregisters and the whole group keeps the existing unpinned fallback. Setup or registration exceptions and incomplete rollbacks fail startup only after all workers have finished the transaction. The unpinned fallback also forces the DMA copy path so a GPU kernel never dereferences pageable host memory. ## Related Work This does not duplicate the existing host-registration PRs: - #50070 keeps registration and pending-error cleanup on the same CUDA runtime handle, but does not coordinate workers or make their pinning state coherent. - #51081 splits very large registrations into chunks to avoid the 512 GiB registration ceiling, but does not coordinate concurrent worker outcomes. - #51956 adds XPU host registration and platform dispatch, but does not address mixed pinned and unpinned CUDA/ROCm workers sharing one mmap region. This PR is scoped to serializing registration across the TP x PCP x PP workers that share an engine mmap, making one group-wide decision, rolling back partial success, and selecting a safe DMA path after an unpinned fallback. ## Test Plan - Exercise two local Gloo processes for all-success, return-code failure, registration setup exception, and registration exception outcomes. - Verify ordinary fallback unregisters successful workers exactly once and rollback failures retain registration ownership for cleanup. - Verify model-rank ordering spans TP x PCP x PP without crossing DP engines. - Verify unpinned CPU-to-GPU transfers select the DMA implementation. ## Test Result - Diff whitespace validation passed. - Python AST parsing passed for both changed files. - An isolated semantic smoke test passed for model-rank ordering, collective ordering, coherent rollback, setup failure, and rollback failure. - The focused pytest suite could not start because the prepared checkout did not contain pytest, and dependency installation was unavailable. The added tests should be run in CI with: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \ -k "pin_mmap_region or model_parallel_coordination or unpinned_cpu_to_gpu or worker_uses_model_parallel_coordination" \ -q ```
