signal.title: Mamba-2 Triton kernels crash with illegal instruction on SM121 (DGX Spark) without CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
signal.text: ## Bug: Mamba-2 Triton ops produce `cudaErrorIllegalInstruction` in async mode on SM121 ### Environment - **GPU:** NVIDIA GB10 (SM121) — DGX Spark - **Driver:** 580.126.09 - **CUDA:** 13.0 (forward compat 13.1) - **vLLM:** 0.17.2rc1.dev7+g9c7cab5eb (eugr/spark-vllm-docker prebuilt wheels, March 17 2026) - **PyTorch:** 2.10.0a0+a36e1d3 (NGC 26.01) - **Triton:** 3.6.0 - **Model:** `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4` (NemotronHForCausalLM, hybrid Mamba-2 + Transformer + MoE) - **Platform:** aarch64 (Grace CPU) ### Description NemotronH models that use Mamba-2 layers crash with `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered` during inference on SM121 GPUs. The crash originates in vLLM's **Triton-based** Mamba ops (not the `causal-conv1d` / `mamba-ssm` packages, which are not used by vLLM). Setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` makes the model fully stable but **degrades throughput from ~14 tok/s (expected) to ~8.8 tok/s** (~37% penalty) and limits GPU utilization to ~60%. ### Crash location The error surfaces at `mamba_mixer2.py:127` in `forward_native`: ``` x_grouped = x_grouped * torch.rsqrt(variance + self.variance_epsilon) ``` But with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` we confirmed this is an **async error from a preceding Triton kernel** — the actual crash is in one of: - `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py` (`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`) - `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_chunk_scan.py` (`_chunk_scan_fwd`) - `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_chunk_state.py` (`_chunk_cumsum_fwd_kernel` / `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel`) - `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_state_passing.py` ### Call chain ``` NemotronHForCausalLM.forward → NemotronHDecoderLayer.forward (Mamba layer) → MambaMixer2.forward → torch.ops.vllm.mamba_mixer2 → conv_ssm_forward (Triton kernels: causal_conv1d_fn, mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen, selective_state_update) → self.norm(ssm_output, gate) ← async error surfaces here ``` ### Key findings 1. **Individual Triton SSM kernels work in isolation** — `_chunk_cumsum_fwd` passes with correct tensor shapes 2. **Basic Triton JIT kernels work on SM121** — simple `@triton.jit` pow/mean kernels run fine 3. **The crash only happens in async mode** — `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` makes everything stable 4. **Targeted `torch.cuda.synchronize()` after `conv_ssm_forward` does NOT fix it** — the issue is at the CUDA driver dispatch level, not Python-level synchronization 5. **`CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1` causes deadlock** at engine startup (profiling phase) 6. **CUDA graphs are incompatible** — `--enforce-eager` is required alongside `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` because the sync patch inside `conv_ssm_forward` breaks graph capture 7. **The native `causal-conv1d` 1.6.1 package compiles and works for SM121** — but vLLM doesn't use it (uses its own Triton reimplementation instead) 8. **llama.cpp / Ollama achieve ~14 tok/s on the same hardware** with their own CUDA kernels — the issue is specific to vLLM's Triton Mamba ops ### Workaround ```yaml env: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING: "1" command: | vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \ --enforce-eager \ --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \ --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ ... ``` Result: stable at **8.8 tok/s** (vs ~14 tok/s expected). ### Suggested fix directions 1. **Preferred:** Investigate the Triton code generation for SM121 async execution — there may be a missing memory barrier or wrong PTX target in the JIT output for the Mamba kernels 2. **Alternative:** Allow vLLM to optionally use the native `causal-conv1d` / `mamba-ssm` CUDA kernels (which work on SM121) instead of the Triton fallback, similar to how flash-attn can be swapped for different backends 3. **Minimal:** Add per-layer `torch.cuda.synchronize()` only around Mamba ops when running on SM12x, instead of requiring global `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` ### Related issues - #36821 — No sm_121 support on aarch64 - #35519 — NVFP4 illegal instruction on SM121 (fixed by PR #35947 for E2M1, but Mamba ops remain broken) - #31128 — Add support of Blackwell SM121 - #37030 — Marlin kernel wrong token on SM121 ### Performance impact | Config | Decode tok/s | GPU util | |--------|-------------|----------| | `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `--enforce-eager` | 8.8 | ~60% | | Ollama (same model, same hardware) | ~14 | ~90%+ | | Expected (no workaround) | ~14-17 | ~90%+ |

### 🐛 Describe the bug # vLLM crash: deterministic null-pointer GPU fault in NVFP4 MoE path on GB10/Blackwell (`modelopt_mixed` + marlin + fp8 KV) ## Summary Serving `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` (FP4 MoE, `quantization=modelopt_mixed`, `moe_backend='marlin'`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`) on a single NVIDIA GB10 (Grace-Blackwell, CUDA 13.0), the V1 engine dies intermittently (~every 1.5–2.5 days of continuous serving) with a CUDA memory-access error surfaced at `async_copy_ready_event.synchronize()`. The engine enters `EngineDeadError`, every in-flight request 500s, and the process shuts down. The **device-level fault is deterministic and identical across independent process restarts and across a vLLM version bump** — the same compute-class method offset, the same data word, and a null (`@ 0x0`) `FAULT_PTE`. This is not hardware (no ECC/contained-error Xids; a bit-identical fault value across three separate crashes rules out random corruption). It points to a **null/optional pointer that is dereferenced on a specific code path** in the FP4-MoE (or fp8-KV) kernels. **Upgrading `0.25.1 → 0.26.0` did not change the fault at all** — the GPU-level signature is byte-identical before and after. ## Environment - **Platform:** NVIDIA DGX Spark Workstation - **GPU:** NVIDIA GB10 (Grace-Blackwell / Blackwell, `sm_121`), unified memory, CUDA 13.0 - **Host:** Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17, aarch64 - **vLLM:** reproduced on **0.25.1** and **0.26.0** (identical fault on both) - **torch:** **2.11.0** (CUDA 13 wheel; `nvidia-cudnn-cu13`, `nvidia-nccl-cu13`, `nvidia-cusparselt-cu13`, `nvidia-nvshmem-cu13`), bundled `triton` - **Quant / kernel stack in the venv (any of these may own the faulting kernel):** `nvidia-modelopt`, `compressed-tensors`, `llmcompressor`, `auto-round`, `flashinfer-python`, plus custom kernel packages `humming-kernels`, `quack-kernels`, `tilelang`, `tokenspeed-mla` - **Model:** `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` (MoE, 40 layers, NVFP4 weights) - **Engine:** V1, `uniproc_executor`, TP=1, PP=1 ### Serving config (from the engine's `dump_input.py` config dump) ``` dtype=torch.bfloat16 max_seq_len=32768 quantization=modelopt_mixed kv_cache_dtype=fp8 enforce_eager=False cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE moe_backend='marlin' linear_backend='auto' enable_prefix_caching=True enable_chunked_prefill=True tensor_parallel_size=1 served_model_name=fpx-brain ``` ## Observed behavior The Python traceback is always the same and reflects the *async* nature of the CUDA error (the faulting kernel is reported at the next synchronize, not at launch): ``` File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 313, in get_output self.async_copy_ready_event.synchronize() File ".../torch/cuda/streams.py", line 254, in synchronize super().synchronize() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: misaligned address ``` On other instances of the *same* fault, torch classifies it as `illegal address` instead of `misaligned address`. Both are the CUDA runtime's surface labels for the same underlying device fault (see dmesg below), so the torch-level label is not a reliable discriminator. ## Device-level evidence (`dmesg | grep Xid`) — the important part Across five crash clusters, two Xid signatures appear. **Family A** is the dominant one and is **bit-identical across independent PIDs and across the 0.25.1 → 0.26.0 upgrade:** ``` # Family A — crash under 0.25.1 (pid 1890909) Xid 13: Graphics Exception: channel 0x2, Class 0000cec0, Offset 00000510, Data 001c62ac Xid 31: MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC2 GPCCLIENT_GCC faulted @ 0x0_00000000. Fault is of type FAULT_PTE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ # Family A — crash under 0.25.1 (pid 2036909) Xid 13: Graphics Exception: channel 0x2, Class 0000cec0, Offset 00000510, Data 001c62ac Xid 31: MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC1 GPCCLIENT_T1_2 faulted @ 0x0_00000000. Fault is of type FAULT_PTE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE # Family A — crash under 0.26.0 (pid 3814664) <-- after the upgrade Xid 13: Graphics Exception: channel 0x2, Class 0000cec0, Offset 00000510, Data 001c62ac Xid 31: MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC1 GPCCLIENT_T1_10 faulted @ 0x0_00000000. Fault is of type FAULT_PTE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ ``` Key points: - **`@ 0x0` + `FAULT_PTE`** = a **null-pointer dereference** by a compute kernel, both read and write variants observed. - **`Class 0000cec0`** = the Blackwell compute class; **`Offset 00000510` / `Data 001c62ac`** are identical across all three Family-A crashes — a *deterministically computed* bad value, not random heap corruption. - No ECC / uncontained-error Xids (48/63/79/94/95) anywhere → **not a hardware fault**. **Family B** (one occurrence) is the same defect surfacing under **cudagraph replay** — instead of a single-channel null fault it becomes a grid-wide out-of-range storm ending in a channel reset: ``` Xid 13: Graphics SM Warp Exception on (GPC 0..3, all TPC/SM): Out Of Range Address Xid 13: Graphics Exception: ESR ... =0x1c81fb60 ... (same faulting PC 0x1c81fb60 on every SM) Xid 43: channel 0x2 reset (pid 2574477) ``` Every SM in every GPC faults at the **same PC `0x1c81fb60`**, consistent with a single kernel launched grid-wide reading a corrupt/stale pointer captured into a CUDA graph. Interpretation: **one bug, two faces.** Eager execution → the null deref faults immediately as Family A (single channel). Cudagraph replay → a stale captured pointer turns it into the grid-wide Family B storm + reset. ## Batch state at the fault (from the scheduler dump) Captured at the 0.26.0 crash: - 22 running requests; **mixed batch**: one chunked-prefill tail (`num_scheduled_tokens=40`, computed 2096/2136) + 21 single-token decodes; `total=61`. - `kv_cache_usage ≈ 0.166`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`. - `new_block_ids_to_zero=[388]` — a **fresh KV block being zeroed on the faulting step**. - `has_structured_output_requests=false`, `structured_outputs=None` — **guided/structured decoding is NOT involved** (ruled out as a cause). ## Suspected location A null/optional device pointer dereferenced on a specific path, most likely one of: 1. **FP4-MoE (`marlin`) grouped-gemm** — a per-expert scale/weight/routing pointer that is null/unallocated when an expert is selected but receives zero tokens in a given batch (empty-expert edge case), consistent with the reproducible `Data` word and null fault. 2. **fp8-KV path** — a KV scale pointer on a freshly-zeroed/newly-allocated block (note `new_block_ids_to_zero` on the faulting step), triggered at a paged-block boundary in a mixed chunked-prefill + decode batch. ## What we've already ruled out - **Hardware / dying GPU** — no ECC Xids; bit-identical fault value across three crashes and a version bump. - **The version** — `0.25.1` and `0.26.0` produce the identical Family-A device signature. - **Guided/structured decoding** — `has_structured_output_requests=false` at the crash; the fault reproduces with no structured-output requests in flight. - **`--enforce-eager`** — does not remove the underlying null deref; it only collapses Family B (grid-wide reset) back into Family A (single-channel fault), i.e. reduces blast radius, not frequency. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [ROCm][AMD] Kimi-K3 Gap and Roadmap Tracking
signal.text: Kimi-K3 is a very successful launch. This issue is to track vLLM upstream work for feature enablement and performance optimization on ROCm. <details><summary>Day 0 features/baselines</summary> - AITER fused-moe: a16w4 (GENERAL) and a8w4 (INTERLEAVE ) were integrated for performance. Flydsl/opus a8w4 is perf is 3.5% higher than flydsl a16w4. - AITER MLA attention: non-causal mla-gluon kernel was used for 12 head. - AITER triton conv2d - AMD vendor specific KDA - DSpark speculative decoding: Target model used AITER MLA (gluon) and draft model used TRITON_MLA. Perf improvement on lower concurrency (c1-c16). - Day 0 docker: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3 - Day 0 recipes: https://recipes.vllm.ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3?hardware=mi355x&features=reasoning - vLLM upstream PRs for day 0 K3 code: #50000 [#50089](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50089) [#50090](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50090) </details> **Feature Gaps**: - [ ] fp8 kv-cache-dtype support: Needed to avoid AgentX performance degradation. - asm-mla path: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51040 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51011 - gluon-mla path: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50619 - - [ ] gfx950/MI350 distributed inference: Required for multi-node K3 enablement and scaling. - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51052 - [x] DSpark: prefix-caching needs work - https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4474 - [ ] offloading performance/compatibility: Needed for offloading support and agentic workload. - cpu offloading + rocm 7.14/7.15 - [x] Dependency: 1. signal.title: [Bug] Fix cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice in fused_add_rms_norm for T…
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR fixes a critical bug where `fused_add_rms_norm` and `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant` kernels threw `cudaErrorSymbolNotFound` (CUDA Error 13) on older architectures like SM 7.5 (Turing) when using `bfloat16`. **Root Cause:** The bug was caused by a compiler mismatch between the Host and Device compiler passes in `nvcc`. The previous kernel signatures used `std::enable_if_t` (SFINAE) predicated on `_typeConvert<scalar_t>::exists`. Because native `bfloat16` is only supported on SM 8.0+, the SFINAE condition evaluated differently on the host vs. the device for SM 7.5. This caused the compiler to generate different mangled symbol names for the host-side stub vs the device-side cubin. Furthermore, attempting to parse the discarded optimized execution branch on SM 7.5 caused a hard compilation error inside `_f16Vec`, which forced `nvcc` to silently drop the SM 7.5 kernel entirely. **Fix:** 1. Unified the kernel template signatures by removing SFINAE and using `__global__ void` to guarantee identical symbol mangling across architectures. 2. Moved the conditional execution into the kernel body using `if constexpr`. 3. Added dummy types to the base `_typeConvert` template in `type_convert.cuh` to satisfy `nvcc`'s strict parsing of discarded `if constexpr` branches on SM 7.5, preventing the compiler from silently dropping the kernel. **AI Assistance Attribution:** Per the project's contributing guidelines in `AGENTS.md`, AI assistance was used during the debugging process to diagnose the NVCC SFINAE mangling bug and to structure the `if constexpr` fallback logic to prevent hard parsing errors on older SM architectures. The submitting human reviewed all changed lines and ran the relevant tests end-to-end to verify the fix. Fixes #<YOUR_ISSUE_NUMBER_HERE> ## Test Plan Ran the complete IR layernorm test suite on a Tesla T4 (SM 7.5) to ensure all parameterizations (including `bfloat16` / `dtype1`) compile and execute successfully. ```bash pytest tests/kernels/ir/test_layernorm.py ``` ## Test Result **Before:** The `bfloat16` parameterized tests consistently threw fatal symbol lookup errors when attempting to launch the kernel on Turing hardware: ```text RuntimeError: CUDA error: symbol not found CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call... ``` **After:** All tests pass cleanly with zero failures. ```text ========== 1442 passed, 184 skipped, 16 warnings in 848.15s (0:14:08) ========== ``` --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: fix: Enable FlashInfer GDN prefill on SM12x
signal.text: ## Purpose Enable FlashInfer's GDN prefill backend for CUDA SM12x when the existing vLLM requirements are met: `linear_key_head_dim == 128` and CUDA runtime 13 or newer. vLLM already selects this backend for Hopper and SM10x, but falls back to Triton/FLA on SM12x. Current FlashInfer has a dedicated SM120 GDN prefill dispatch, so the vLLM selector is narrower than the backend it guards. This is a path-specific selector change, not a claim that every Blackwell kernel supports every SM12x device. The in-tree CuteDSL GDN backend remains SM10x-only. ## Why this is not duplicate work Searched open and closed vLLM PRs for SM120/SM12x GDN prefill and FlashInfer GDN backend selection. - #31740 and #34822 propose broader Blackwell platform classification helpers; they do not add this path-specific GDN selector support. - #51954 optimizes ordinary GDN decode gate handling, not prefill backend selection. No separate PR found by those searches implements this focused change. ## Changes - Allow the FlashInfer GDN prefill selector on SM10x or SM12x, preserving the existing head-dimension and CUDA-runtime requirements. - Keep the in-tree CuteDSL GDN selector limited to SM10x. - Add selector tests through the real `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend` production function. This revision drops the previously bundled GateLinear, MambaMixer2, ReplaySSM, and online NVFP4 SM120 gates. Those are independent capability questions and are not covered here. ## Tests ```bash PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py -q ``` Result: `6 passed`. The cases verify: - SM120 selects FlashInfer for both `auto` and explicit `flashinfer`; - SM120 does not select the SM10x-only CuteDSL backend; - the existing SM100 CuteDSL behavior remains; - CUDA 12 and a non-128 key-head dimension still fall back to Triton. Targeted red/green: temporarily removing the SM120 selector change made the two SM120 FlashInfer cases fail (`2 failed, 4 passed`). Restoring the change returned `6 passed`. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed. ## SM120 measurements (dual RTX 5090, ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B-FP8, TP=2) FlashInfer 0.6.16 on this machine dispatches its SM120 GDN prefill DSL kernel (`arch_major == 12`). Serving logs show `Using FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128)`. **Correctness.** A FlashInfer-versus-Triton/FLA kernel matrix passed 19/20 characterized cases, including all 10 cases at this model's TP=2 geometry (8 key / 24 value heads, dim 128). The sole miss was final-state mean error 0.0006321 vs a 0.0006000 limit borrowed from the CuteDSL GDN test. Both kernels stayed close to a stepwise FP32 reference. The limit was not loosened. **Quality (bounded).** Thinking-off chat, GSM8K questions 0–7, graphs on: Triton and FlashInfer both 8/8 correct with 8/8 restart answer agreement. Generated wording differed (token IDs 1/8). This is a non-regression screen, not a full GSM8K score and not thinking-on eval. **Throughput on this setup — no speedup.** Nospec, thinking off, c=1, unique salt (cold prefill), streaming TTFT. FlashInfer vs Triton/FLA: | Workload | Triton | FlashInfer | |---|---:|---:| | ~8k cold prefill, 1 output, TTFT | 2.059 s | 2.055 s (~0.2%) | | ~2k cold prefill, 1 output, TTFT | 0.542 s | 0.552 s (FI ~2% slower) | | cached ~128 prompt, 256 output, decode tok/s | 75.2 | 72.4 (~3.7%) | The 8k prefill comparison was the place a GDN-prefill kernel win should appear. It did not. Decode is a different kernel and was a control. This PR does **not** claim a performance improvement. Hopper and SM100 use different FlashInfer GDN kernels than SM120; those were not measured here. ## Limitations - SM12x FlashInfer GDN prefill still requires `linear_key_head_dim == 128` and CUDA 13, same as SM10x. - Other SM100-gated paths (GateLinear, Mamba/ReplaySSM tuning, online NVFP4) are unchanged. - Kernel comparison is compatibility-positive, not a clean 20/20 under the borrowed threshold. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex / Cursor Grok were used for implementation support, duplicate-work research, tests, and measurement harnesses. I reviewed the changes and am responsible for the submission.

signal.title: [PP][XPU]Overlap async-scheduling PP sampled-token broadcast with compute
signal.text: When async scheduling is enabled with pipeline parallelism (`pp > 1`), the sampled token ids produced by the last PP stage are sent back to the first stage via `torch.distributed.broadcast` on the PP device group. This broadcast was issued as a blocking collective (`async_op=False`) on the default compute stream. ## Purpose This PR makes that broadcast non-blocking (`async_op=True`) and defers the `.wait()` to `_prepare_input_ids`, right before the received tokens are actually consumed. All token-independent work now can overlaps. ## Test Result Server: python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model openai/gpt-oss-20b \ --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-util=0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --max-num-batched-tokens=8192 --max-model-len=6144 -pp 2 -tp 2 Client: vllm bench serve --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --dataset-name sonnet \ --dataset-path benchmarks/sonnet.txt --sonnet-input-len=4096 \ --sonnet-output-len=1024 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 90 \ --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 18 --temperature 0 Running the gpt-oss-20B Output token throughput (tok/s) can improve from 338 to 448 on XPU device

signal.title: [Frontend] shutdown engine core and its sub processes asap when initializing
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> PLEASE FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE ENSURING ALL CHECKLIST ITEMS (AT THE BOTTOM) HAVE BEEN CONSIDERED. ## Purpose This is a follow up after #43417. After #43417 merged, if a frontend process exits unexpected, for example, in a multi api process setup env, `run_multi_api_server` will call `finally` and engine core proc manager shutdown function will be called. For now, engine core proc has been busying in initializing model executor processes and engine core process has not register a custom signal handler. Thus, a SIGTERM signal will be sent to engine core process and engine core process will exit and leaving its subprocess, model executor processes, as they are. Finally these model executor processes will only exit when they run to an exception or completion wasting GPU resources. We need to shutdown engine core process and all its subprocesses asap. ## Test Plan 1. setting `export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=120` 2. run `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --max-num-seqs 512 --renderer-num-workers 1 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline_parallel_size 2 --data-parallel-size 1` ## Test Result a log will be record soon after the timeout exception is raised. ``` RuntimeError: Frontend process failed during engine core initialization. See root cause above. Failed frontend proc(s): {'ApiServer_1': None} DEBUG 08-14 08:25:07 [v1/utils.py:605] [shutdown] Process manager: start process_count=2 timeout=5.0s names=ApiServer_0,ApiServer_1 INFO 08-14 08:25:07 [v1/utils.py:615] [shutdown] Process manager: send sigterm to process ApiServer_0 DEBUG 08-14 08:25:08 [v1/utils.py:647] [shutdown] Process manager: complete DEBUG 08-14 08:25:08 [v1/utils.py:605] [shutdown] Process manager: start process_count=1 timeout=5.0s names=EngineCore INFO 08-14 08:25:08 [v1/utils.py:615] [shutdown] Process manager: send sigterm to process EngineCore (EngineCore pid=2441) INFO 08-14 08:25:08 [v1/engine/core.py:1317] [shutdown] EngineCore: trigger received signal=SIGTERM WARNING 08-14 08:25:13 [v1/utils.py:635] [shutdown] Process manager: force killing remaining processes count=1 WARNING 08-14 08:25:13 [v1/utils.py:640] [shutdown] Process manager: force killing remaining process EngineCore pid 2441 ``` --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signal.title: [Perf][Nemotron] Skip redundant latent-MoE all-reduce at TP>1 (~13% decode win)
signal.text: ## Purpose **Nemotron-3 decode regressed ~13% between v0.26.0 and v0.27.x at TP>1. This PR restores it.** | tp4, concurrency 1 | v0.26.0 | v0.27.1 | v0.27.1 + this PR | |---|---|---|---| | inter-token latency | 4.08 ms | 4.60 ms (+12.8%) | **4.07 ms** | | output tok/s per user | 245.0 | 217.2 (−11.4%) | **246.0** | No existing issue — I searched issues and PRs for "latent MoE all-reduce" and "routed_output_transform" and found nothing related. ### Affected models when tp=4, bs=1, ISL/OSL=1000 | ckpt | v0.27.1 vs 0.26.0 regression | |---|---| | nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 | −13.83% | | nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 | −15.36% | ### Root cause [`_maybe_reduce_routed_output_before_transform()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L434-L453), added in v0.27.0rc1, all-reduces the routed output in latent space *before* `routed_output_transform` is applied, since that transform may be non-linear. [The combined output is then all-reduced again](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L455-L495) on the late path. So **every latent-MoE layer at TP>1 or EP>1 issues two tensor-parallel all-reduces per token instead of one** ([call site](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L742-L749)). The function does not exist in v0.26.0. `NemotronH` is hit because it passes [`fc2_latent_proj` as its `routed_output_transform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L226). ### The fix The early reduce is only needed when the transform does not commute with the sum over ranks. A bias-free linear transform does commute — `sum_r W x_r == W sum_r x_r` — so reducing once *after* it is equivalent and costs one collective instead of two. With a bias it does not, since `sum_r (W x_r + b) == W sum_r x_r + R*b`. This adds an opt-in `reduce_commutative` attribute on the transform, **defaulting to `False` so every model that does not set it is byte-for-byte unchanged.** `NemotronH` sets it from `not config.mlp_bias`; its [`fc2_latent_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L194-L201) is a `ReplicatedLinear`, identical on every rank. **Kimi K3 is unchanged.** Its [`KimiRoutedOutputTransform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py#L295-L302) wraps an `RMSNorm`, which is non-linear and genuinely needs the early reduce. It never sets the attribute, so both collectives are retained. <details> <summary>Interactions checked, quantised transforms, and the alternative considered</summary> **Interactions with the surrounding reduce logic** - [`skip_final_all_reduce`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L468-L473) asserts against [`self._fused_output_is_reduced`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L403-L408), a property of the combine kernel that this PR does not touch, so the assertion is unaffected. - For `NemotronH`, `reduce_results` defaults to `True` — the [`reduce_results=False`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L180) nearby is on the *shared_experts* MLP, not the FusedMoE — so `skip_final_all_reduce == False` and the late all-reduce always fires. **Quantised transforms** When the transform is quantised, input quantisation is a non-linear step, so `sum_r T(x_r)` and `T(sum_r x_r)` differ by more than float summation order. This is not introduced by this PR — it is what v0.26.0 did for those checkpoints — but stating it plainly: commutativity holds exactly for the unquantised bias-free linear case, and to within quantisation error otherwise. Measurements below are bf16. **Alternative: wire NemotronH to `LatentMoERunner`** [`LatentMoERunner`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L52) already implements a fused single-collective path, and pointing `NemotronH` at it would also remove the extra collective. I did not pursue it because: 1. It now lives under `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`, moved there by [#50678](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50678) ([`b9d1e2437e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/b9d1e2437e1ad6d98d301939949072b5c56dfef1)) after v0.27.1 — upstream has deliberately scoped it to K3. 2. It assumes K3's transform shape, reading [`transform.norm` and `transform.up_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L216-L224), whereas `NemotronH` passes a bare `ReplicatedLinear`. It would need an adapter — a larger blast radius than this guard. Happy to be redirected. The attribute name/API is a bikeshed I have no attachment to; a `Protocol` or a flag on `FusedMoEConfig` would work as well. </details> ## Test Plan 4x GB300 (sm_103), stock upstream containers `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0` and `:v0.27.1`, no NCCL env overrides. Public checkpoint [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16) (`moe_latent_size=1024`, `mlp_bias=false`). Every flag below exists in both releases, so the arms differ only by vLLM version. ```bash # 1. Serve (--tensor-parallel-size 1 for the negative control) vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \ --served-model-name nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-model-len 2200 --max-num-seqs 128 \ --attention-backend FLASHINFER --trust-remote-code \ --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \ --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --port 8000 # 2. Benchmark (aiperf 0.12.0), C over 1, 8, 32, 64 aiperf profile --url localhost:8000 --model nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b \ --tokenizer nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \ --endpoint-type completions --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --streaming \ --extra-inputs "min_tokens:1000" --extra-inputs "max_tokens:1000" \ --extra-inputs "ignore_eos:true" \ --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 1000 --synthetic-input-tokens-stddev 0 \ --output-tokens-mean 1000 --output-tokens-stddev 0 \ --concurrency ${C} --request-count $((5 * C)) --warmup-request-count 1 # 3. Accuracy (server as above but --max-model-len 4096) lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 ``` Controls: **tp1** (the early reduce is gated on `tp_size > 1 or ep_size > 1`, so tp1 must show no change); **same-node** v0.26.0 vs v0.27.1, with v0.27.1 also run on a second node to quantify node variation; patch state asserted per run by reading the installed `moe_runner.py` / `nemotron_h.py` out of `site-packages`. ## Test Result ### tp4 concurrency sweep Two runs per arm at concurrency 1; run-to-run range was 0.00 ms. | inter-token latency (ms) | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 | |---|---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | 4.08 | 6.23 | 9.88 | 12.18 | | v0.27.1 | 4.60 | 6.63 | 10.39 | 13.09 | | v0.27.1 + this PR | **4.07** | **6.11** | **9.88** | **12.21** | | v0.27.1 regression | +12.83% | +6.51% | +5.18% | +7.47% | | output tok/s per user | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 | |---|---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | 245.02 | 160.72 | 101.25 | 82.13 | | v0.27.1 | 217.17 | 150.85 | 96.26 | 76.42 | | v0.27.1 + this PR | **246.00** | **163.70** | **101.18** | **81.90** | v0.26.0 performance is restored at every concurrency. The win is largest at low concurrency and shrinks as batch grows — expected, since at small batch these collectives are latency-bound so their *count* dominates, while at larger batch they become bandwidth-bound and the surviving reduce (4096-wide hidden dim) is larger than the removed one (1024-wide latent dim). It is not a trade-off at any measured point. ### Controls - **tp1 negative control:** ITL 6.22 ms (v0.26.0) vs 6.20 ms (v0.27.1), −0.30%. No difference, as the TP gate predicts. - **Node-to-node variation:** v0.27.1 on two different GB300 nodes, 4.63 vs 4.60 ms — 0.65%, far below the 12.83% effect. ### Accuracy — gsm8k, 5-shot, greedy, tp4, full 1319 questions Both arms on the same node in the same container, differing only by this patch: | arm | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---| | v0.27.1 stock | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9181 ± 0.0076 | | v0.27.1 + this PR | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9166 ± 0.0076 | +0.0008 and −0.0015, i.e. 0.1 and 0.2 standard errors — no measurable difference. Bitwise identity is not expected: moving the all-reduce past a linear map changes floating-point summation order. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. Documentation: no update needed — no public API change, no new model, and the `reduce_commutative` contract is documented in the docstring of `_maybe_reduce_routed_output_before_transform`. </details>

signal.title: [V1][Bugfix] structured_output × spec-decode: pre-commit grammar filter for boundary-step bonus tokens
signal.text: ## Summary In speculative decoding with a reasoning parser + structured output, post-boundary bonus tokens leak into the response stream as garbage prefixes before the valid JSON (e.g. `chunk_0{"...": ...}`, `**{"...": ...}`). This PR adds a pre-commit grammar filter so those tokens never enter request output. Generalizes the fix direction in #36138 (single-token boundary, post-commit `accept_tokens`) to: - **multi-token reasoning markers** (e.g. gpt-oss's Harmony `<|channel|>final<|message|>`, which is 3 tokens after tokenization and almost never lands fully inside a 2-5 token speculative batch); and - **the post-commit-vs-output-stream ordering** — the existing `should_advance` deferral correctly suppresses the post-commit `accept_tokens` call on the boundary step (avoiding spurious `FINISHED_ERROR`), but the bonus tokens are already in `_output_token_ids` by then. Credit to @sfbemerk for the original analysis in #36138; this lands the same fix idea via a pre-commit path so it composes with the existing `should_advance` deferral instead of replacing it. Closes #43338. ## Root cause The grammar bitmask is gated on `reasoning_ended` (see `StructuredOutputManager.should_fill_bitmask`). The boundary step's bonus tokens are sampled **without** the mask engaged — `reasoning_ended` is `False` at sample time and only flips `True` after the boundary is observed (i.e. after this step's tokens are sampled). So the bonus token at the post-boundary position can be any free-text continuation the verifier's logits prefer (`chunk`, `**`, `(no`, etc.). The existing `should_advance` deferral logic (lines 348-368 on `main`) correctly handles the matcher state — it defers FSM advance to the next step so the matcher doesn't try to accept the boundary-step's pre-boundary reasoning tokens. But it does nothing about the post-boundary bonus tokens that are already in the response stream. ## Mechanism `precommit_filter_tokens(request, new_token_ids) -> (filtered_new_token_ids, num_rejected)`: 1. Returns early unless the request uses structured output, has a reasoner, and `reasoning_ended` is still `False` (this only fires on the boundary step). 2. Calls `_find_reasoning_end_in_tokens(new_token_ids, prior_token_ids=request.all_token_ids)` to locate the boundary index. The detector uses `reasoner.is_reasoning_end_streaming` with progressively longer cumulative prefixes, so multi-token markers spanning the prior-context / batch line are detected (same approach as `should_advance`). 3. If a boundary is found, splits `new_token_ids` into `(pre_boundary, post_boundary)` and dry-runs `grammar.validate_tokens(post_boundary)` (the matcher state is unchanged on return; only the accepted prefix is reported). 4. Calls `grammar.accept_tokens(req_id, validated)` on the validated prefix so the matcher reflects the committed JSON head when the next step runs. 5. Returns `(pre_boundary + validated, len(post_boundary) - len(validated))`. Scheduler wiring (24-line insert before `_update_request_with_output`): ```python if new_token_ids: new_token_ids, num_grammar_rejected = ( self.structured_output_manager.precommit_filter_tokens( request, new_token_ids ) ) if num_grammar_rejected > 0: if request.num_computed_tokens > 0: request.num_computed_tokens -= num_grammar_rejected if request.num_output_placeholders > 0: request.num_output_placeholders -= num_grammar_rejected ``` The `num_computed_tokens` / `num_output_placeholders` decrement mirrors the existing verifier-rejected-spec-token bookkeeping in `Scheduler.update_from_output` (lines 1361-1373), so the next step re-runs from the truncated position with the grammar mask now correctly engaged. ## Test results Reproducer: gpt-oss-120b on 2× H100 with `--reasoning-parser openai_gptoss` + `--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens":3, ...}'` + `response_format: {"type":"json_schema","strict":true,...}`. 300 real production prompts. | Variant | clean | prefix_bled | malformed | HTTP 500 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | vLLM `main` HEAD (this PR's base, unpatched) | 64 (21%) | 163 (54%) | 73 (24%) | 0 | | vLLM 0.20.1 (pre-PR baseline) | ~140 (47%) | ~156 (52%) | — | 0 | | #36138 HEAD (sfbemerk fork) | 184 (61%) | 0 | 0 | **116 (38%)** | | **This PR** | **285 (95%)** | **0** | 15 | **0** | This PR is running in our production cluster on top of `v0.21.0` for ~3 hours, ~5K live requests, no regressions observed. The 15 malformed in the 300-trace shadow are not bleed — they're long responses hitting `max_tokens=2000` mid-JSON (unchanged from baseline). The `#36138` row above shows the post-commit `accept_tokens` path: when the matcher rejects the boundary-step's free-text bonus tokens, it sets `FINISHED_ERROR` → HTTP 500. By moving validation pre-commit and truncating instead of failing, this PR avoids both the 500s and the bleeds. ## Scope of change `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`: +120 lines (two new methods, additive). `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: +24 lines (one block inserted before `_update_request_with_output`). Total: +144 lines, 0 deletions. No existing API changed. No behavior change when `speculative_config is None` (the boundary detector returns `None`, the filter returns inputs unchanged). ## Notes for review - Same-step `accept_tokens` in `precommit_filter_tokens` and the existing post-commit `accept_tokens` in `update_from_output` are mutually exclusive: pre-commit fires only when `reasoning_ended` is still `False` and a boundary is found in-batch; post-commit fires (via `should_advance`) only when `reasoning_ended` is already `True`. No double-advance. - The `should_advance` deferral (`Defer FSM advance until the next pass`, lines 356-365) is preserved and still correct: pre-commit handles the boundary step's post-boundary slice; deferred post-commit handles all subsequent steps with the mask engaged. - Happy to add a unit test exercising the boundary-mid-batch + grammar-rejection path against a `MockReasoner` + `MockGrammar` if the maintainers prefer that before merge. ## Test plan - [ ] CI passes - [ ] Unit test added (will follow if reviewers want one — let me know) - [ ] Re-test against `main` post-merge to confirm

signal.title: [Bug][KV Offload] cudaHostRegister can leave mixed pinned/unpinned TP ranks
signal.text: ## Summary CPU KV offload can start a tensor-parallel group in a mixed pinned/unpinned state because each rank independently calls `cudaHostRegister` for its own process VA of the shared mmap and failures warn-and-continue locally. ## Observed behavior Across two independent TP=2 hosts, each with 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, repeated starts produced both: - both ranks pinned; and - mixed starts where one rank failed registration and continued unpinned while the other rank remained pinned. The pinned rank carried the expected page-table bookkeeping asymmetry: 96 MiB/GPU for a 48 GiB region (`48 GiB / 4 KiB * 8-byte PTE`). Synchronized transfer performance is then bounded by the unpinned rank while the pinned rank still pays the bookkeeping cost. ## Desired invariant A TP group should never serve with mixed host-registration state. Registration needs a coordinated all-rank outcome: - every rank pinned; or - every rank consistently follows the same configured fallback/failure policy. A rank-ordered registration transaction with a mapping fence removes simultaneous registration as a source of nondeterminism. If any rank fails, successful ranks must unregister exactly once before the group makes one coherent policy decision. ## Policy question Current behavior preserves availability by allowing local unpinned fallback. Changing every failure to a startup error could break valid deployments whose regions cannot be pinned (for example, the large-region failure discussed in #51080). The durable fix therefore needs an explicit compatibility decision: coherent all-unpinned fallback versus a configurable `require_pinned` policy. This issue reports the mixed-state invariant only. It does not propose changing the CUDA error-drain ownership tracked in #50070. AI assistance was used to help analyze and reduce this report; the hardware observations and invariant were verified by Ottley Engineering.

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Register the offload region in chunks
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51080. `pin_mmap_region` registers the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call. A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` no matter how much host memory is free, so `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 is never pinned. Measured on 4×H200 NVL with 1.3 TB free, one process, no model loaded: | region size | result | |---|---| | 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB | | 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s | | 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** | | 600e9 | fails, code=2 | This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank. Our production config (GLM-5.2, TP4/DCP4, `cpu_bytes_to_use=600e9`) stopped starting. Chunks end on block-row boundaries. Rows are page aligned (`kv_bytes_per_block % PAGESIZE == 0` is asserted in `SharedOffloadRegion`), so the driver's page rounding never makes two registrations overlap, and no single block transfer spans a boundary. Registration time scales with the bytes registered, so splitting one call into several costs nothing. On failure the chunks registered so far stay pinned rather than being rolled back — transfers through them keep the fast path, and the warning now says how much of the region was pinned. `cudaHostUnregister` takes the pointer a registration was made with, so cleanup releases each chunk. Not a duplicate: #50070 drains the latched CUDA error that a failed registration leaves behind (which is why this used to surface as a bogus `AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` in `warm_v1_block_table_kernels`); it does not change what gets registered. The two are complementary and touch the same function, so whichever lands first leaves a small mechanical conflict for the other. Deliberately out of scope, same shape but not reachable in practice today: `ECSharedRegion.pin_memory` and `simple_kv_offload/cuda_mem_ops.py::pin_tensor` register in one call too, but those regions are orders of magnitude smaller. ## Test `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` — three tests covering chunk boundaries, a failure part way through, and a failure on the first chunk, with `cudaHostRegister` mocked and the chunk cap lowered to two pages. ``` python3 -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py -q # 30 passed ``` The ceiling itself was measured on the 4×H200 box with the standalone probe above. An end-to-end run of the patched build at `cpu_bytes_to_use=600e9` is queued for our next maintenance window; I'll post the result here. AI assistance (Claude) was used for this work; all changes reviewed.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix divergent warp collectives in partial NeoX QK-Norm+RoPE
signal.text: ## Summary ## Author: Drew Jin, SJTU & Qwen Team, <drewjin0827@sjtu.edu.cn> Solving Issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51049 This PR fixes silent Q/K corruption in the partial-NeoX path of `fused_qk_norm_rope`. When `rotary_dim < head_dim`, the multi-head-per-warp kernel produces incorrect Q/K values for every head after the first in each warp chunk. On H200, `token_heads_per_warp=8` can additionally produce NaNs. Verified against `upstream/main` at commit `005fa017566177e1a66d75eba7908d326c5acd60`. ## Root cause In the NeoX branch, only the rotary lanes entered the RoPE section, while the branch invoked warp collectives using the full-warp mask: ```cpp if (laneId < rotary_lanes) { __syncwarp(); rotated = __shfl_xor_sync(FINAL_MASK, value, pairOffset); __syncwarp(); } ``` For partial RoPE, `rotary_lanes < warpSize`. Therefore, `FINAL_MASK` names lanes that do not execute the collective, which is undefined behavior. `warpReduceSum` itself is not the issue. In the packed kernel, the invalid RoPE collective occurs before the next head’s RMSNorm reduction, causing the observed corruption in subsequent heads. The single-head kernel contains the same latent UB, but it has no following packed-head iteration that exposes the failure. ## Fix The NeoX shuffle is now executed by every lane named by `FINAL_MASK`. Only rotary lanes consume the shuffled value, access the cos/sin cache, and update the rotated elements. The fix is applied to both the single-head and multi-head-per-warp kernels. The implementation retains the platform-specific `FINAL_MASK` rather than constructing a narrowed 32-bit mask. This preserves the existing CUDA and ROCm wave64 mask semantics and avoids undefined expressions such as `1u << 32`. ## Tests Added regression coverage for the previously untested packing paths: - Force `token_heads_per_warp` to `1`, `2`, `4`, and `8`, and compare each variant directly against the existing unfused PyTorch reference. - Cover `head_dim ∈ {64, 128, 256}`, `rotary_ratio ∈ {1.0, 0.5, 0.25}`, NeoX and interleaved layouts, and fp16/bf16. - Verify that the V segment remains bitwise unchanged. - Verify that packed and auto-selected outputs are bitwise identical to the single-head implementation. - Exercise the SM90 auto-selected pack4 and pack8 paths with large-token inputs. Verified on NVIDIA H200 (SM90). `compute-sanitizer` racecheck and synccheck are clean. Because these tools do not report this divergent-mask UB, the regression is enforced by numerical tests. ## Impact The QK-Norm+RoPE Inductor fusion is currently opt-in and disabled by default, so this issue does not affect default vLLM inference. The observed packed-head corruption requires all of the following: 1. per-head Q/K RMSNorm routed through this fused operator; 2. NeoX-style RoPE; 3. partial RoPE (`rotary_dim < head_dim`); and 4. dispatch to the multi-head-per-warp kernel. On SM90 with `head_dim <= 128`, the dispatcher at the target commit uses: ```text U = num_tokens × (num_q_local + num_kv_local) U < 10240 → token_heads_per_warp = 1 10240 ≤ U < 40960 → token_heads_per_warp = 4 U ≥ 40960 → token_heads_per_warp = 8 ``` Large prefills can therefore enter the affected packed paths. Confirmed partial-NeoX configurations include GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7, Ring-1T, and the partial-RoPE attention layers in Step-3.5-Flash and Laguna-XS.2. Full RoPE, interleaved RoPE, and models not routed through this fused operator do not trigger this issue. ## Performance The fix also removes the slowdown observed in the affected packed path. Benchmark configuration: ```text GPU: NVIDIA H200 (SM90) PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA: 13.0 dtype: bf16 head_dim: 128 Q heads: 16 KV heads: 4 Timing: CUDA events Warmup iterations: 30 Measured iterations: 300 Statistic: latency per call ``` | Tokens | Pre-fix auto | Post-fix auto | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2,048 | 22.5 µs | 15.9 µs | 29% | | 8,192 | 68.5 µs | 43.9 µs | 36% | | 16,384 | 125.6 µs | 80.1 µs | 36% | The single-head path is essentially unchanged. ## ROCm ROCm was not tested. The patch preserves the existing platform-specific `FINAL_MASK` and wave64-compatible code path; it does not introduce a CUDA-specific 32-bit active mask. ## AI assistance This PR was developed with AI assistance. I reviewed all changed lines, validated the behavior on H200, and understand the implementation and test coverage.
signal.author: drewjin

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Scale UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs groups by DCP
signal.text: ## Purpose #49964 gated the DCP scaling of a group's token span on `isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, AttentionSpec)` so that Mamba groups stay unscaled. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` is a container rather than an `AttentionSpec` subclass, so DSA models — whose indexer and MLA layers merge into a single uniform group — lost the DCP factor too: - `build_offloading_config` reports `tokens_per_block = block_size` (64), - `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` still returns `block_size * dcp` (128) for a single group, so enabling CPU offload under DCP dies at startup: ``` AssertionError: tokens_per_block=64 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=128. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes. ``` Reported by @Leoyzen on GLM-5.2, TP8/DCP2, `fp8_ds_mla`, MTP, `OffloadingConnector`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46514#issuecomment-5166406963 The scaling is now keyed off a helper that unwraps the container, so Mamba groups stay unscaled and every attention group keeps its DCP span. Same call site is fixed in `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` for multi-group configs. Related: #50823 fixes the other half of the same container-not-unwrapped family (block table width). ## Test Three tests, one per call site plus the hybrid case, next to the Mamba tests from #49964: - `offloading_connector/test_config.py::test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_attention_group_blocks` - `offloading_connector/test_config.py::test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_group_alongside_mamba` - `core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_resolve_block_sizes_scales_uniform_type_group_by_dcp` Verified fail→pass in a container built from the current nightly (`0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f`); each test fails on unpatched `main` with the reported assert (`tokens_per_block=16 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=32`) or a wrong span, and the two suites pass with the fix: ``` python3 -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -q # 115 passed ``` Config-level change, no effect on model output; no eval run. AI assistance (Claude) was used for this work; all changes reviewed.
